## 2026-10-07 — The DEF4ULT STUDIO ident, and the game opening like WELCOME BACK, HERO

The owner asked for this game to open the way WELCOME BACK, HERO (one_room_dg)
does: the same intro, and the same way of starting it from Godot. Pause, options
and a button redesign follow in their own commits.

**The ident is that game's, not one like it.** scenes/StudioIntro.tscn and
src/ui/studio_intro.gd port its DEF4ULT STUDIO ident - the cue table, easings,
cyan, crest, the two studio sounds and the 5x7 face of the plate - and the five
files it needs are carried byte for byte into assets/studio/ (README there with
their sources and hashes; headless_check holds the hashes). assets/README.md
says why that folder is the one thing under assets/ that is not generated: a
studio ident belongs to the studio. The plate keeps that game's face because
this game's harvest_heading is wider and squarer and the plate would not be the
same plate.

**It is laid out on that game's frame.** The ident was composed for a 1280x720
canvas stretched to the window; this game is 480x270 at whole multiples, and a
300 pixel crest does not fit in 270. So while it runs it puts a 1280x720
fractional frame on the window, with its own black as the clear colour, and
hands this game's frame back the moment it leaves (and in `_exit_tree`, so a
check freeing it halfway cannot strand the window). The proof that it is the
same: src/tools/capture_intro.gd shoots that game's ten capture beats, and at
1280x720 every one of them is pixel-identical to WELCOME BACK, HERO's own
capture_intro.gd - 0 differing pixels in ten frames.

**How it opens.** project.godot's main scene is the ident now and the boot
splash is its black (the two are asserted equal, so the first frame has no
colour click). The ident hands over through the router (`App.goto(TITLE)`), and
when its timeline runs out - not on either skip - the title rises out of the
same black over 0.9 s (`App.rise_from_black`, runtime only). Any key in the
black lead leaves at once; the first key later collapses the tube, the second
leaves; `--skip-intro` skips it. The old 1.6 s icon ident on the title
(boot_ident.gd) is gone - the studio ident replaces it - so the title opens on
PRESS ANY KEY as before, and the crash dialogue no longer waits for an ident.
In the editor, `.godot/editor/project_metadata.cfg` now has
`embed_on_play=false`, the setting WELCOME BACK, HERO has: F5 opens the game in
its own window instead of inside the editor's Game tab. That file is per
machine and not versioned.

## 2026-10-07 — Dawn sends the night home

The owner reported zombies left standing on the farm after dawn, and asked
that at dawn they turn back and leave the screen.

**The bug.** A won night ends only when nothing is left alive, but a lost one
ends on the tick the house falls - with the rest of the wave still in the yard
- and nothing ever took them off the farm. `begin_day()` swept the rubble and
left the zombies: frozen all day (no enemy system ticks in daylight), drawn by
the world view, and standing where they were when the same night came back, so
a retried night began with last night's winners at the door. Reproduced
headless: night 1 lost with 3 standing, still 3 that afternoon, and the
replayed night opened with them plus its first spawn; the autoplayer's lost
nights left 10 to 14 behind.

**The rule.** `Enemies.withdraw()`, called from `Phases.begin_day()`, takes off
the farm everything the night left on it: the survivors, the shots still in
the air, the fires, and the flare (`Ability.put_out()`) - none of which advance
by day, so any of them would have hung over the farm until the next night.
`State.reconcile()` does the same for a save in DAY or PREPARATION with a
zombie in it, which only a save written before this can be; a RESULT still
being read keeps them until its morning.

**The picture.** `EnemyRetreats` (src/ui/enemy_retreats.gd), a cosmetic pool
like `EnemyDeaths`: the world view notes the survivors on the result screen's
ticks and, when the rules remove them at dawn, walks each one away from the
house - the one heading that cannot cross it - at 1.5 times its night pace, in
its own walk frames, facing where it goes, and fades it out over the last two
thirds of 2.4 s, about as long as the dawn change. Nothing in it is saved or
hashed, and a won night leaves nobody to walk.

**And the night's speed is the night's.** SimDriver multiplied the ticks of
every phase by `gameplay/night_speed`, so a night watched at 4x was followed
by a day at 4x - the clock, the crops and the farmer - and the options page's
NIGHT SPEED did the same by day. `SimDriver.effective_speed()` is the chosen
speed at night and one in every other phase, the build step included.

## 2026-10-07 — A plan for the whole game: day, night and the road to 1.0

The owner asked for a plan, in a markdown file, of how the game develops from
here: day earns the money, the night is defended while the farmer sleeps and
the player places the weapons, how many days and nights there are, how it
plays, the items, the farming and the fishing.

`docs/PLANO-DO-JOGO.md`, in Portuguese like `design.md`, because it is the
owner's document to answer and edit. In short: going to bed is the reality
switch; at night a guardian cursor with a free camera places, upgrades, sells
and repairs, and the flare is aimed; the build step waits for START. One year
of 4 seasons x 14 days - **56 days and 56 nights** - with a Full Moon on each
7th and a boss on each 14th (the Giant first, then three new ones), about 10
to 13 hours, then an endless Year 2. Crops grow by days, any grass can be
tilled, 12 crops each with a sale, food or defence role; fish by pond, season
and hour with a small timing minigame and rods; tools in three tiers; coop,
barn and five artisan machines; a shipping bin. 14 defences (6 new), 10
enemies and 4 bosses. The calendar always moves on and a lost boss night
repeats; a night ends at 06:00, the house standing at sunrise wins, and
whoever is left walks off. Nine phases, of which Phase 1 (sleep = night, the
cursor) is the checkpoint the rest waits on; twelve decisions with a
recommendation each; what it changes against `design.md`; the known issues.

Made from an audit of what the code does today - every table in
`game_data.gd` and the rules that read them - so the plan starts from the
real numbers: a 4 minute day, a 20 s build step, three crops that grow in
minutes on 60 soil cells, one fish, no tools, one cow and two chickens for
meat, eight defences, five enemies, ten nights and the endless curve. Two of
its findings were confirmed by reading and are listed for Phase 0: repairs are
measured against the base table, so a levelled tower mends to its level-1 HP
and the house to 100 rather than 140, and the house-untouched money and
technology are measured against 100 too. The rest it suspected from reading
alone, and they are listed as suspected, not fixed: spawn regions that can be
built shut, a mortar with no gunpowder dealing nothing, the flamethrower's
bonuses and ammunition, the can's "/8", barricades laid by day, three stale
documents. The night speed leaking into the day was confirmed and is fixed in
the entry above.

No code changed. Nothing is in the backlog yet: once the owner has answered
section 11, each phase becomes tasks in tools/backlog/.

## 0115 - Spawn ground that cannot be built shut - done 2026-10-07

**The suspicion was real, and cheaper than the plan guessed: ten fences, not
seventeen.** Before the fix, with a fence on every cell of `SPAWNS[0]` (x=68,
y 22-31) placed in PREPARATION and night 1 run to its end, seeds 115, 2024 and
777 all read: `Waves.size_of` 12 (all twelve from the east), spawned 0, killed 0,
breaches 0, alive 0 - and the night **won** after 1093 ticks. `Enemies.spawn`
found no free cell, returned 0, and `Waves.tick` counted each member as sent.
Fix chosen: **the deterministic fallback, inside `Enemies.spawn_cells`** (still
the one place that answers where one can stand). A region with no free reachable
cell answers the nearest free ground around it, ring by ring outwards, and of
the first ring with anywhere to stand only the cells farther from the house, by
the flow field, than the line cell they are beside (when there are any). Why
this over the alternatives: a placement refusal only covers fences *on* the
line - a ring of impassable towers around it seals it just as well - and a
member that waits for a free cell needs a new state key and a bound; the
fallback closes both ways of sealing with no new state, no new string and no
wait. One bar for the whole line was tried first and was too low: (68,22) and
(68,23) sit on the road home at field distance 26, which let the house side
(x=67, distances 27-31) in; per-cell bars leave exactly the 12 cells of x=69
plus the two ends (68,21) and (68,32). After the fix the same three seeds
spawned all 12; the undefended house fell at the tenth breach (begin_night
resets it to `house_full`, so the reproduction's 100000 did not survive
nightfall) with 2 still alive - 0 + 10 + 2 = 12. The search always ends at the
porch at worst (never buildable, beside the door); `spawn()` returning 0 is now
only "nowhere on the farm reaches the house" and it `push_error`s rather than
losing the member quietly. A region with one free cell left answers exactly
that cell, so the spawn draw (one `Rng` call per member placed) is unchanged
and the determinism scenario, which seals nothing, gives the same SIM. No state
key, so nothing for `initial()`, reconcile or `State.TABLES`: a save with a
sealed region spawns by the same rule (asserted through a var_to_bytes trip).

## 0116 - The mortar and the flamethrower, empty and upgraded - done 2026-10-07

**All of the suspicions were real**, each reproduced through `Towers.tick` with
a scratch script before any fix (deleted after):
- **Empty mortar**: placed in PREPARATION, powder gone, a walker 6 tiles out -
  one shell fired and landed, walker 20 -> 20. The unarmed shot is
  `SHAPE_SINGLE` but stays ballistic, and a ballistic landing passed no target.
  Fix: a ballistic landing carries its `target`, and a single shape hits it if
  it is still alive. **Decision: the rock hits the one it was thrown at, not
  whoever is on the aimed cell** - a shell flies 45 ticks and a walker crosses a
  tile in 20, so the aimed cell is two tiles behind it on landing and the
  cell-only rule would leave the empty mortar nearly silent, which 0035 forbids;
  `Juice` already reads a landed shot as landing on its target. Now 20 -> 8
  (`Ammo.weak_damage(40)` = 12) and the walker beside it untouched.
- **Flame reach**: with 'long barrels' the tower aimed at a walker at 4 tiles,
  spent a round and burnt nobody (cone used the raw range 3). Now `reach_of`.
- **Flame damage**: level 3 with 'true sights' dealt 5, `damage_of` says 6. Now
  `damage_of(state, entry, armed)`. **Decision: `burn_damage` is not scaled** -
  the node says every tower *hits* a fifth harder, and 2, 3, 4 x 1.2 round back
  to themselves anyway, so scaling would be a rule with no effect today.
- **Flame rounds**: 10 s on a full pool, 19 shots, 19 rounds. `ammo_every_ticks`
  (60) is now read by `Towers._load()`: one round lights 60 ticks of firing, a
  countdown `ammo_lit` on the occupant, charged `reload + 1` ticks per shot, no
  `Farm.touch`, absent in old saves = light the next round. Now 19 shots, 5
  rounds. `ammo_every_ticks` carries `# LEVER: ticks, 1-4 seconds worth`;
  `check_defences` refuses it without `ammo` or under `reload_ticks`.

after midnight; `DHUD_DUSK` still read). `WorldView` reads the hour: dawn ->
noon (06:00-12:00), noon -> dusk (12:00-18:00), then the dusk light deepening
towards the night ramp until 02:00, at most half way (`EVENING_DEPTH`, view
only); the night ramp is unchanged. No rule reads dusk, so SIM does not move.

`_case_0039_clock`'s "starting near the top of it" now looks for 06:0, and its

before the end of the day, which now is deep evening. shot.gd's `noon` is
12:00 on the clock (it was half the day, which is 16:00), so its field is

## 0127 - Going to bed starts the night - done 2026-10-08

What changed: going to bed is the reality switch (plan section 12). The
`begin_night` intent is now `sleep`, written by the GO TO BED button, the
`night` key (id kept, so saved bindings survive; `ACT_NIGHT` reads GO TO BED /
IR DORMIR), the bed, the title backdrop and every tool and test.
`Phases.go_to_bed(state)` - DAY only, refused with an error otherwise - runs
`begin_preparation`, and **`begin_preparation` sets `house_visit.asleep`**, so
every road into the build step (bed, button, 0128's pass-out, `NightRoad`)
leaves him asleep; asleep is not `House.inside` (`begin_preparation` still
calls `House.leave`, so building and the world view carry on outdoors).

bed's `HOUSE_FURNITURE` rectangle, side by side) and `House.can_sleep`;

past dusk "GO TO BED - NIGHT %d" / "IR DORMIR - NOITE %d"; it only asks by day.

produced for hours nobody lived (no exploit). It is what the night button
already did, so it needed no new code - only this line, a comment on
`Phases.go_to_bed` and the assert.

## 0130 - The night camera - done 2026-10-08

What changed: from the build step until the morning the camera is the
player's. `main.gd`'s new `_steer_camera` follows the farmer by day as before.
The first frame outside DAY hands the camera over (`aim_night_camera`) and
opens it on the house. Then `WorldView.pan_camera` moves it with
`pan_direction()`, which reads three inputs:
- the move keys (WASD, the arrows, and the left stick and d-pad bound to them);
- the right stick through four new actions;
- the pointer inside a `CAMERA_EDGE_PIXELS` band at the window's edge, only
  while the window has the focus and the pointer is in it. Both are tracked
  from the window's own `focus_*` / `mouse_*` signals, and the pointer from
  `main._input`, read and never consumed.

A diagonal is no faster than a straight line, and everything is clamped by
`_camera_bounds`, with no zoom. Nothing pans while the pause menu is up or on
the result, which leaves the camera where it was; the morning snaps it back to
the farmer, and he is followed from there.

`CAMERA_PAN_SPEED` (240 world px/s, `# LEVER` 120-480) and `CAMERA_EDGE_PIXELS`
(8, 4-16) are scalars beside `TRANSITION_SECONDS`, out of `digest()` like it
(view feel, not balance). The speed is in real seconds: 2x/4x do not use
`time_scale`, so `delta` is real.

**The right stick's actions**: `pan_left` / `pan_right` / `pan_up` / `pan_down`
are in `project.godot` (right stick axes 2 and 3, no keyboard default - the
move keys pan at night) and in `InputActions.ACTIONS` under `ACT_GROUP_NIGHT`.
Their strings are `ACT_PAN_*`: LOOK LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN, OLHAR À ESQUERDA/À
DIREITA/PARA CIMA/PARA BAIXO. The sync, the clash and 0121's "no two actions
on one pad input" checks pass. **No pad input is left over now** (0136's prompt
already says so): `_case_0121_pad`'s rebind of interact onto the right stick is
now first refused, naming LOOK UP. The test then frees the stick by hand
(`apply()` builds from the photograph and gives it back, which is asserted).
The owner's unstaged `run` re-serialisation in `project.godot` stays out of the
commit: the committed copy is HEAD plus the four actions.

**The shots' camera hook**: `shot.gd`'s `_look_at(cell)`. By day it walks the
farmer there as before; from the build step on, `Main.aim_night_camera` puts the
camera on it (nowhere = the house). The comment that said the camera cannot be
set is rewritten for the day only. `dusk` (through `_a_sown_field`), `wave` and
`result` (the defence line) and `passed_out` (where he fell) use the hook. The
night no longer tries to walk him (0129 made the wave shot spend 61 stuck
ticks). The shots turn `edge_pan` off, since their real pointer is anywhere.

  (0.08 s), out of `digest()`. `WorldView.keep_in_view` makes the camera follow

## 0132 - Defences go down only at night - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the plan's decision 4. The day earns and the night spends.

**The phase rule** (`Building.allowed_in_phase`):
- A `DEFENCES` id is allowed only in PREPARATION and NIGHT, a `BUILDINGS` id
  only in DAY.
- The new `Building.why_not_now(state, id)` gives the reason. A defence by
  day answers `WHY_ONLY_AT_NIGHT` (the row existed); a building after dark
  answers `WHY_NOT_AT_NIGHT`. `why_not` uses it.
- `why_not_upgrade` follows the same rule. Its `WHY_MID_NIGHT` refusal is gone,
  because the plan (4.3) lets upgrades go on during the waves; the row left
  strings.csv once nothing read it.
- Selling follows too: the new `Building.why_not_sell(state, cell)`, which
  `sell` checks first.
- `catalogue()` still follows `allowed_in_phase`, so by day B lists the four
  production buildings and at night the eight defences.

**The barricade** lost `placeable_at_night`, and `check_defences` lost the rule
that tied that flag to a lifetime and a nightly limit. The barricade keeps both
as its own identity (cheap, temporary, limited). Section 13's bug stays out of
the build step, which has no clock after 0136, in two ways:
- `Building.forget_tonight` moved from `begin_night` to `begin_preparation`, so
  a barricade put down in the build step counts against tonight's limit.
- One put down before the waves gets a pending `lifetime` instead of
  `expires`. The new `Building.start_lifetimes` (called by `begin_night`, cells
  in index order) winds it, so it stands for `lifetime_ticks` after the waves
  begin.

**The cursor at night**:
- `BuildMode`'s `upgrade` and `remove` already write `build_upgrade` and
  `build_sell` at `build_cell`, which is the cursor's cell from the build step
  on (0131).
- `main._cursor_look` now shows the upgrade look over something of the
  player's that can go up a level, and the sell look over one that can only go
  back to the ledger.
- `_case_0131_cursor`'s "the cell it filled reads blocked" became "reads sell":
  a wall has no levels.

**The tutorial**:
- `build` follows `night` in `TUTORIAL`, and `Sim._tick_preparation` runs
  `Tutorial.tick` on its beat.

## 0133 - The hotbar of defences - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the night's shop window. `src/ui/hotbar.gd` (new, `Hotbar`) runs
along the bottom from the build step to the morning.
- **Its slots.** One slot per id of `Building.catalogue(state)`, in its order
  and never from a list here, so phase 13's defences get slots with no edit.
- **Where it sits.** 40x32 slots from (4,215): under the log's four lines,
  over the ammo line at 248, and stopping before x 330 where the night HUD's
  bottom-right controls start. That makes 8 to a page; more go on pages, and
  the page shown is the one holding the selection.
- **What a slot shows.** A005's 16x16 icon over two short lines of price:
  - the kit count (`HOTBAR_KITS` "x%d") when a kit is banked;
  - else the cost, as "25i 10o" over "20w";
  - or, greyed and red, what is short;
  - for a thing with a nightly limit, the allowance (`HOTBAR_LEFT` "%d/night"
    / "%d/noite").
- **Its tooltip** is `Describe.defence` (name, cost, HP, damage, range out of
  `GameData`).
- **Picking a slot.** A click, `slot_1`..`slot_8` on the current page, or
  `hotbar_prev` / `hotbar_next`, wrapping. All go through `Building.select`.
  `cancel` clears through `BuildMode` as before. The text palette is by day
  only now (buildings); at night the refusal it used to print rides on the
  cursor's tooltip whenever the cursor reads blocked.
- **The price line's spacing** is two new `UiKit` label variations,
  `SlotPrice` (warm) and `SlotShort` (red). A theme override in the screen
  failed `headless_check`'s "no screen overrides the theme".

**The icons** go through 0120's road. `PlaceholderArt.ART` now also takes
texture stand-ins:
- `"stand_in": &"buildings/gun_tower"` means `res://sprites/buildings/gun_tower.png`;
- `bare` marks a static file with no frame number (`icon_wall.png`, as A005
  delivers);
- each stand-in is drawn shrunk into the 16x16 box.

There are eight `icon_<id>` entries for A005. `tools/placeholders.py` reads
`bare` and checks a stand-in's file: 68 stand-ins over 9 packs. 0131's
registry assert counts its own A003/A004 entries.

**The pad had no free button** (0121's layout plus 0130's right stick), so it
was reshuffled; the reasons are written into `_task_0121_pad`'s exceptions:
- LB/RB go to `hotbar_prev`/`hotbar_next`, the genre's bumpers, as the prompt

- `remove` went to R3, because a deliberate click is the safest home for a

## 0134 - Repairing by cursor - done 2026-10-08

What changed: repairs at night are made by pointing.

**The confirm:**
- From the build step to the morning, confirming the guardian's cursor (a
  click, or A on a pad - 0133's confirm) on anything `Repair.can_mend` allows
  writes 0129's `repair_cell`. It does so whatever is in the hotbar.
- Any part of a multi-cell building mends its anchor.
- `Building.tick` spends the cell through `Repair.apply_all`, as far as the
  ledger covers, at `Repair.cost_at`'s price (the house at its own percent),
  up to 0113's real maximum.
- One rule, `GuardianCursor.mend_target(state, cell)`, decides both the repair
  look and the confirm. `BuildMode` takes the confirm while build mode is up,
  and `Main._unhandled_input` takes it otherwise.
- **Found by a failing test:** the confirm read the look the previous frame
  had drawn, so a click that moved the cursor onto the house was judged
  against wherever it had been. The cursor now takes a mouse press's cell in
  `_input`, before anything handles the press, and the confirm works out the
  target from that cell.

**The cursor and its tooltip:**
- The cursor shows its repair look (A004's flame brackets and hammer) over
  anything mendable; something to mend comes first.
- The tooltip adds `Describe.repair_line`: what a full repair costs and how
  many of the missing hit points the ledger covers (`CURSOR_REPAIR`, "mend
  all: %s - %d of %d HP paid for" / "consertar tudo: %s - %d de %d de vida
  pagos"). Like `under_cursor`, it only reads.
- The five `CURSOR_` rows (0131's four and this one) were moved into key order
  in strings.csv; 0131 had put them after the `DEF_` rows.

**The farmer's verb:** `Interact._offered` no longer offers `repair` on a
`DEFENCES` id. It stays on the house, the production buildings and the
stations; a damaged wall by day offers nothing and waits for the night. This
was gated in `_offered`, as the prompt asked, and not added to `DAY_ONLY`.

**The interim REPAIR button of 0129 is gone** from the night HUD, along with
its `NHUD_REPAIR` row. The flare and the speed keep their places until 0139.

**The siege, measured** with a scratch probe (`siege_probe.gd`, deleted). Seed
3505 has a wall column across the walkers' road; 6000 ticks is the cap, and
"held" means the wall stood all 200 s.

| Walkers | Alone | Old held key (1 HP per 3 ticks, about 10 HP/s) | Cursor, once a second |

| 1 | falls at 303 | falls at 849, 10 stone | held, 112 stone |

What changed: the flare goes off where the player aims it.

**The rule** (`src/core`):
- `intent` gains a level, `ability_cell` (`[-1, -1]` is nowhere), which
  reconcile fills in old saves.
- `Ability.use` centres on it. Nowhere or off the farm is refused before
  anything is spent: no cooldown, no `flares`, and the press is consumed all
  the same.
- 0129's interim house centre is gone.

**The aim** (`src/ui`):
- `Main._drive_cursor` writes `ability_cell` every frame from the guardian's
  cursor, like `build_cell`, and nowhere when there is no cursor.
- The ability key (F, RT on a pad) fires on the press at the cursor.
- The night HUD's FLARE button now **arms** it (`GuardianCursor.arm`) and
  lets go of its focus, so a pad's next A confirms. The next confirm, a
  click or A, fires at the cursor (`confirm_flare`, which comes before
  repair and placement in both `BuildMode` and `Main`), and `cancel`
  disarms (`cancel_aim`, before build mode's or the pause menu's escape).
- While the flare is ready and the button is armed or the key held, the
  cursor reads `aim` (A004's moon look) and draws the reach. That is
  `ABILITY.radius_tiles` round its cell, a Chebyshev square, the cells
  `Ability.use` hits (`reach_cells`): code, like the route preview.
- **Note:** with the key firing on its press, as the prompt asks, the
  key-held preview lasts only as long as the key is down before the flare
  goes off. The armed button is where the preview lives. 0139's hint line
  is the place to revisit it.

**Found by the aim test: a day press queued a flare.**
- `Ability.tick` runs only at night, so F pressed by day stayed in `intent`
  and went off on the night's first tick, wherever the cursor happened to be.
- `_case_0054_ability` presses F by day on purpose. Before this task the
  stale flare went off on the house, and the victim happened to stand beside
  it.

  comment is gone.

  - the line and the slow aim at the house;
  - `_count_the_flares` aims at the house and counts only flares that went

- 0129's `_task_0129_asleep` expects the flare on its aimed cell.

## 0136 - The build step waits for START - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the build step has no clock. It waits for START, except after a
pass-out, when the horde is at the gate and gives thirty seconds.

**The rule:**
- `intent` gains the edge `start_waves`.
- `Sim.tick` reads it and clears it on every tick, so a press by day or at
  night is simply gone. `_tick_preparation` spends it through 0118's
  `Phases.start_waves`.
- `Phases.build_step_ticks` is now 0 ("no clock") after going to bed, and
  `PASS_OUT_PREPARATION_TICKS` after a pass-out. That timer is the only one
  left, and START may still come sooner.
- `PREPARATION_TICKS` left `game_data.gd` and `digest()`. The day clock stays
  stopped through the build step, as it was.

  in the bar.

NOITE"):

  `headless_check` controls group, `_case_0095` and 0121's
  "interact on J keeps its A".
- `project.godot`'s commit copy is HEAD plus these changes; the owner's
  unstaged `run` change stays in the working copy only.

**The road**: `NightRoad.through_build` presses START (`press_start`) and steps
the one tick it lands on. `build_ticks_left` is that one tick, or zero

## 0137 - The night ends at 06:00 - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the night has an end known in advance. A house still standing
at dawn wins, and killing everything sooner still does.

**The rule:**
- `NIGHT_TICKS := 240 * SECONDS` (`# LEVER` 180-300 s) is the waves' length,
  the same after a bedtime and after a pass-out. `validate()` keeps it below
  `Sim.MOST_TICKS_IN_A_NIGHT`.
- `Waves.begin` writes `wave.dawn_at`. Its `initial()` is `NIGHT_TICKS`, so an
  old save gets a whole night; `Phases.ticks_to_dawn(state)` reads it.
  `NightRoad.park` puts dawn out of reach, so parked nights never end.
- `Sim._tick_night` ends the night last, after `Combat.tick`
  (`_test_for_dawn`): still NIGHT at `dawn_at` gives a `dawn` event (`walked`
  = how many are still on the farm), `Rewards.settle(true)` and
  `enter_result(true)`, with the survivors left on the farm.
  `begin_day`'s `Enemies.withdraw` walks them off.
- A house at 0 still loses on its own tick, and `_test_for_the_end` still
  wins early. **Interim until 0153:** dawn does not end a night while
  `Combat.boss_here`, and the countdown holds at 0:00.
- The `dawn` event is a new `Events.KINDS` entry, `good` in `log_panel.gd`,
  with `LOG_DAWN` ("dawn - %d walked off" / "amanheceu - %d foram embora")
  and a sample in `_task_0090_log`.

**Inside the night:**
- `Waves.schedule_ticks(record)` is a night's sending time, counted the way
  `Waves.tick` spends it.
- `check_nights` refuses any night still sending within `DAWN_MARGIN_TICKS`
  (`# LEVER` 60 s, 30-120) of dawn. Both levers joined the `time` row of
  `digest()`.
- **The endless curve did not fit.** At the house pace, night 28 sent until
  206 s and night 40 until 302 s, past dawn itself. A generated night that
  would still be sending at `NIGHT_TICKS - DAWN_MARGIN_TICKS` now carries
  its own `interval_ticks` (`Endless._fit_before_dawn`): the largest member
  spacing that fits, down to one a tick. `Waves` reads it through
  `interval_in`, and the authored ten keep the house pace.
- Nights 11-40 on seeds 0/1/7 now all send by 179 s, which `_task_0137_dawn`
  samples from the schedule functions alone.

**`python tools/nights.py`** prints each night against the night. Dawn is at
240 s and every night must be sent 60 s before it:

|---|---|---|
| 1 | 36 s | 203 s |
| 2 | 42 s | 198 s |
| 3 | 56 s | 183 s |
| 4 | 67 s | 172 s |
| 5 | 77 s | 162 s |
| 6 | 82 s | 157 s |
| 7 | 78 s | 161 s |
| 8 | 84 s | 155 s |
| 9 | 82 s | 158 s |
| 10 | 78 s | 161 s |

**The night HUD** counts down `NHUD_DAWN` ("DAWN 3:54" / "AMANHECER 3:54") on
the strip's right, never as a wall clock. It is capped at a whole night, so a
parked fixture does not show nonsense. Skip and 1x/2x/4x simply run to dawn.

**Tests:**
- `_task_0027_the_loop`: "the night ended at dawn or with everything dead,

- `_task_0055_speed`: "skipping never runs past dawn".
- `_case_0082_shots`' `Sim.skip_night` says it runs to dawn at the latest.

## 0141 - Teaching the new night - done 2026-10-08

What changed: day one now teaches the new night - go to bed, set something
down in the build step, press START, hold till dawn. It does it by watching
the state, and it never gates anything.

**The steps** (`GameData.TUTORIAL`) are now nine: chop, plant, water, sell,
craft, then `bed`, `build`, `start` and `dawn`.
- The old `night` step ("N, or the button") became the bed step, and
  `TUT_NIGHT` left strings.csv.
- **`MAX_TUTORIAL_LINES` went from 7 to 9**, the top of its range. No two day
  steps were merged: each of them still teaches one thing. `check_tutorial`
  passes.

**What finishes each step** (`Tutorial._happened`, reading the state only):
- `bed`: asleep seen (the bed, the button, or 02:00);
- `build`: a defence standing, which since 0132 means one placed in a build
  step;
- `start`: NIGHT reached;
- `dawn`: a night won, at dawn or with nothing left alive (0137 made those the
  same).

**`Tutorial.tick` runs on its beat in the night too**, and never indoors.
`PerfNames.NIGHT` gains `Tutorial`, so the benchmark now times
`night_tutorial`. The new row has no baseline, which `perf.py` does not
compare.

**Taught where it belongs** (`Tutorial.current_here`, `TAUGHT_IN`): the first
unfinished step of this part of the day.
- The day's five and the bed's are taught by day, build and START in the
  build step, and dawn in the night.
- So a stall never visited no longer keeps the build line off the build step.
- `current()` still orders `is_finished` and `progress`.

**Where each line points** (`Tutorial.anchor_of` and `points_at`):
- **bed**: the farmhouse door while he is out on the farm, and the bed
  itself in the house view (`HouseView.room_to_screen`).
- **build**: open ground a third of the way from the house to the nearest
  spawn cell. That is read off `GameData.SPAWNS`, not
  `Enemies.spawn_cells`, which rebuilds the path field and so would write
  from a view.
- **START**: the line sits above the button, clear of the hotbar, with the
  pointer down at START.
- **dawn**: the line sits under the strip, with a "^" up at the countdown.
- `tutorial_prompt.gd` resolves the two controls by name through
  `NightHud`. In the house it shows only the bed's line. It hides while the
  bed beat plays, and is now up in the build step and the night (it was day
  only before, so 0132's build line never showed).

**Lines** (both languages; every `TUT_*` row is now measured by
`tools/i18n_check.py` at 462 px, the prompt's width):
- `TUT_BED`: "Done for the day? Sleep in the bed in the house, or press GO TO
  BED."
- `TUT_BUILD`, rewritten: "Pick from the bar below and set it between the
  house and the dark."
- `TUT_START`: "When it is all set, press START. Nothing comes until you do."
- `TUT_DAWN`: "Keep the house standing until dawn - the countdown is up top."

They are practical lines, and none of them uses the words 0041 keeps out
(wave, defence, zombie...).

**Tests:**
- `_task_0141_tutorial` (headless_v1) jumps `dawn_at` rather than playing the
  night.
  - A scripted first day completes every step up to START, in the order of the
    lines. The night held to dawn then completes the last one, and the
    tutorial is finished on day 2.
  - The same script on a farm whose player read nothing - every line done
    before the day starts - reaches the same night and the same morning, hash
    for hash, apart from `tutorial`.
  - Each night line's anchor and place are checked: the door, the bed, open
    ground off the house, START, and the countdown.
- `_case_0141_tutorial` (input_v1):
  - the bed's line after the day's five, with its pointer over the bed in the
    house;
  - the build line in the build step, then START's, its pointer down at
    START and the line clear of the hotbar;

## 0142 - The autoplayer sleeps too - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the autoplayer plays the game as it now is, and keeps playing
after a loss. A night of it is:
- the day;
- to bed;
- the build step, through the intent road;
- START;
- the night to its own end;
- the morning report confirmed.

The balance tools measure the real loop again.

**The loop** (`src/tools/autoplay.gd`):
- **`_a_day`.** The day starts from 0138's wake: out of the door first.
  - It gathers, crafts, buys technology and puts up stations by day only.
  - It goes to bed through the `sleep` intent, at the policy's `bed_minute`,
    or sooner if nothing is left worth doing.
  - Every policy now declares `bed_minute`. All four use
    `DEFAULT_BED_MINUTE`, 01:30, the pass-out warning's minute. It is before
    02:00, so the robot never passes out by accident, which 0128 had only
    avoided by stopping one tick short.
- **`_a_build_step`.** The defence goes down through the intent road, a tick
  a press: `repair_cell`; `Building.select` and then `build_cell` with
  `build_place`; `build_cell` with `build_upgrade`.
  - Each press is checked to have done something, so a refused one is
    planned around rather than spun on.
  - Then `start_waves`. The build step has no clock after a bedtime, so the
    ticks cost nothing.
- **`_a_night`.** `NightRoad.run_night`, capped at `NIGHT_TICKS` and a margin
  of one more night. The margin is for a Giant holding dawn back.
- **`_one_night`** puts the three together and confirms the report. It
  returns the night's row: `night`, `held`, `ended` (`dawn`, `cleared` -
  everything dead first - `house`, or `cap`), `house`, `walked`, `spent` and
  `towers`.
- **`play`** plays `nights_wanted` nights and carries on after a loss.
  - `died_on` is the first night lost, and `nights_won` how far it got
    anyway.
  - `won` means no loss over the nights asked for.
  - It stops only when the run is over or a night is still going at the cap.
- Nothing is placed by day: the policies keep their lists, and their
  defences wait for the build step.

**The report** (`autoplay_run.gd`) keeps what `tools/balance.py` reads:
- the won column and the killer;
- `nights:` as the first night each run lost, or how many it played - the
  same meaning as before, now that a run goes on after a loss.

It adds:
- `won all`: the mean nights won per run over its ten nights;
- under each policy, how its nights ended (dawn, everything dead, house down)
  and how many walked off a night.

**Tests:**
- `_task_0067_autoplay`: one night per policy, down from three runs of four.
  - Each policy declares `bed_minute`, before 02:00.
  - The same seed plays the same night, to the kill, and a different policy is
    a different run.
  - Every row reports `ended` and `walked`, ending at dawn, cleared or house -
    never at the cap.
  - A tower goes up on day one.
  - **A lost night does not end the run.** The robot's own day ends in bed,
    not passed out, and its build step ends with START. A house at 1 HP
    falls. Confirmed, the robot plays day 2, and night 1 comes back.
- `_task_0068_balance`: still one day and one night per policy, through the
  new day, build step and night. All four end the tutorial night cleared, on
  10 house.

**Group times**, measured alone: `_task_0067_autoplay` 7.1 s and
`_task_0068_balance` 7.1 s, 115 asserts between them. `headless_check` as a
whole went from 87.6 s to 72.6 s, most of it 0067's old three runs of four
nights.

**`python tools/autoplay.py`**, the same 100 runs (25 seeds of each policy,
ten nights a run), took 1,411 s before and 2,366 s after.
- First loss: `balanced` night 8 (13x), `economy` night 3 (19x), `towers`
  night 8 (17x), `walls` night 8 (21x). No policy wins all ten, as before.
- Nights won over ten: 6.9 / 6.7 / 6.8 / 7.2.
- Of 1,000 nights, none ended at dawn. Every night held was cleared first:

- Survival per night is identical for `economy`, `towers` and `walls`.

- **The cause is the bed hour, verified.** On seed 9000, a 01:30 bedtime

## 0148 - Checkpoint: is the night better with him asleep? - done 2026-10-08

**The answer: yes - as a night to play. Not yet as a night that lasts.**

Asleep, the farmer hands the whole night to one cursor, and everything the
night asks for is under it. What the night does not do yet is fill the time
the plan gives it: every night played here was over, everything dead, about
a minute into a four-minute night. That is the nights' content, which
0271-0274 write, so their prompts now ask for it (below).

And the same caveat as 0066: **I have played this through synthetic input,
not with hands.** The verdict on how it *feels* - the camera, the cursor at
a desk and on a sofa, whether watching the waves is a pleasure - is still
owed by a person. If that person says no, this task reopens and blocks.

### The nights played

**How.** `src/tools/night_session.gd` (new) drives the real `Main` with
`InputEvent`s - clicks, keys and pad buttons - and never calls a rule in
place of a press. It extends `input_v1.gd` for its harness.
- **The pad is synthetic too.** No pad was attached; the presses are
  `InputEventJoypadButton`/`Motion` through `Input.parse_input_event`.
- **The days are handed over, not played.** Each day's work arrives as a gain
  (60 wood, 40 stone, 40 iron, 30 food, 40 money, 3 tech), because the day is
  not what this checkpoint asks about. So these are four whole nights, not
  four whole days.

One run, seed 20260927, four nights in a row. Played twice, identical both
times, 21 checks and none failed:

| Night | Device | What was done | Ended | House |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | mouse and keyboard | GO TO BED; two gun towers and two walls from the hotbar by click; START; SPEED to 2x; a hurt wall mended by click; FLARE armed and fired by click; a tower upgraded by middle click mid-wave; a wall sold by right click; SKIP; the report confirmed | everything dead (skipped), 54 s in, 12 killed | 100/100 |
| 2 | mouse and keyboard | walked to the bed, SPACE; towers and walls by click, upgraded by middle click where allowed; START by G; 4x | everything dead, 60 s in, 20 killed | 100/100 |
| 3 | mouse and keyboard | still up at 02:00: passed out, a black screen, the 30 s build step; two towers by click; the step ran out on its own; 4x | everything dead, 61 s in, 22 killed | **87/100** |
| 4 | pad only | Back to bed; RB to the gun tower; the D-pad to two cells and A on each; LT upgraded the tower under the cursor; L3 START; Back onto the bar, right to SPEED, A, B; RT's flare at the cursor; 4x; A on the report | everything dead, 72 s in, 40 killed | 100/100 |

- **Nothing walked off and nothing came down** in any of the four.
- **Every report was confirmed,** by click or by the pad's A, and he woke
  inside, beside the bed, each time.
- **The only night the house was touched is the one after passing out.** The
  30-second build step is the cost of staying up, and it shows.

### The autoplayer

`python tools/autoplay.py`, run again for this task: 25 seeds of each
policy, ten nights a run, 1,000 nights in 2,288 s. Seed for seed it is 0142's

| economy | 0 | 167 | 83 | 1.5 | night 3 (19x) | 6.7 |
| towers | 0 | 171 | 79 | 3.7 | night 8 (17x) | 6.8 |

- **No night ended at dawn.** Every night held was held by killing

- **What walks off walks off after a loss.** It is what is still on the

### Against the MVP's night

**Better:**
- **One way in to everything.** Placing, upgrading, selling, mending, the
  flare, the speed, SKIP and START are each a cursor action or a bar button.
  The session reached every one, by mouse and by pad, without the farmer
  taking a step. The MVP's night needed him walked to a wall to mend it, a
  plank at a time (0053), and let only the barricade go down once the waves
  began.
- **The build step is the player's.** After a bedtime it has no clock, and
  START is a decision rather than a timer running out.
- **Staying up has a price you can see.** The short build step after a
  pass-out is the one night the house was hit.
- **A pad plays it all.** Night 4 used nothing else, with no dead end.
- **The morning is one screen.** The report says what happened, and he is up
  and walking the moment it is confirmed.

**Worse:**
- **The night promises dawn and ends a minute in.** The strip counts down
  `DAWN 4:00` and the tutorial says "keep the house standing until dawn". But
  today's ten nights send everything by 36-84 s of a 240 s night (0137's
  table). Every night played here ended with everything dead at 54-72 s, and
  none of the autoplayer's thousand reached dawn.
  - The plan (4.5) wants the opposite: "a night whose length you know in
    advance" and "holding until sunrise is worth as much as killing
    everything", in three to five minutes of waves.
  - Today, dawn and the wall's delaying job (the plan's third reason) do
    nothing.
- **Little to do once the defence is down.** On these early nights the
  house was never hurt except after the pass-out. The one repair here was a
  wall the script knocked about itself. This is the curve's early end more
  than the sleep, and it is the same finding as above.

**Missing:**
- **The walk-off at dawn is never seen.** 0137 walks the survivors off in
  `begin_day`, after the report. 0138 then wakes him inside, behind the house
  view. The plan has it the other way round: they walk off, then the report.
  A player who stays in the house misses it. It does not matter today, when
  no night reaches dawn; it will once 0271 fills the nights. A note for that
  phase: whoever makes dawn reachable should make the walk-off visible.
- **The forecast (0158)** and the guardian's and cursor's art (0145-0147, and
  their packs) are still ahead, as planned.

**Slow or fiddly:**
- **The camera: not judged.** Synthetic input cannot say whether the edge pan
  (8 px) and the pad's pan are comfortable.
- **The pad's cursor** steps a cell a press and repeats after 0.3 s, every
  0.08 s. Crossing twenty cells is under two seconds held; whether that is
  quick enough on a sofa is the hands' question.
- **Found and measured, not a player's problem:**
  - The bar swaps START for FLARE/SPEED/SKIP a couple of frames after START.
  - The hotbar rebuilds its row on the tick after anything is bought, so a
    press and release that straddle that tick select nothing. That takes
    clicking within a thirtieth of a second of a purchase. Measured over
    night 2's waves: no rebuilds in 60 s, because nothing is bought.
  - The session waits for both, and says why in a comment.

### Fixed here

Nothing in the game: no small thing came up that was a bug. The new file is
`src/tools/night_session.gd`, the record of these nights, which can be run
again (`-- --first-night` for the first only).

## 0149 - The calendar: four seasons of fourteen days - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the farm knows what day of the year it is, and says so beside
the clock. No rule reads it yet.

**The rule** (`src/core/calendar.gd`, `class_name Calendar`, node-free,
static):
- `date(state)` is the calendar day. It reads `state["day"]` until 0153 holds
  the calendar still on a boss night, and it is the only place that does.
- The pure helpers are `year_days()`, `year_of(day)`, `season_of(day)` (0-3),
  `day_of_season(day)` (1-14) and `season_id(day)` (`&"spring"` ...). Each
  takes an optional season length, so a test proves a seven-day season
  without turning the lever.
- `season_id` was not in the prompt. It is there so the HUD and every later
  table keyed by season ask one function, not
  `GameData.SEASONS[season_of(day)]` again and again.
- Day 1 is Spring 1 of Year 1, day 14 Spring 14, day 15 Summer 1, day 56
  Winter 14, and day 57 Spring 1 of Year 2. There is no new State key.

**The data** (`game_data.gd`):
- `SEASON_DAYS := 14` (`# LEVER`, 7-28).
- `SEASONS`: the four ids. These are names, not a lever.
- `check_calendar()` in `validate()` refuses anything but four seasons, a
  season named twice, and a season of fewer than two days.
- Both are in `digest()`'s new `calendar` row.

**On screen** (`day_hud.gd`): `SPRING 3` takes the day count's place beside
the clock, one number for the day. `DHUD_DAY` and `DHUD_DAY_FIRST` are gone.
The seasons are named through `Names.KEYS` (`SEASON_SPRING` ...).

**The prompt said `SPRING 3  YEAR 2` on one row. Measured, it does not fit.**
- The date's row has 74 pixels from the label to the purse's icon at 144.
- `PRIMAVERA 14`, the widest date, is 69.
- With the year it is 93 in English and 105 in Portuguese, deep into the
  purse.
- So the year has the line under the date, from Year 2 on: `DHUD_YEAR`,
  "YEAR %d" / "ANO %d". That line is empty by day in Year 1. From dusk the
  evening's line takes it back: dusk, bedtime and the pass-out warning
  matter more than the year.
- There is no `DHUD_DATE_YEAR`. The prompts that named it now say what
  exists: 0158 (the night strip shows the year where it has room) and 0279
  (`SPRING 3` and `YEAR 2` under it), each with its source in

- `DHUD_DATE`'s width column is the real 74.
- `i18n_check` measures a format string unfilled, so the real fit is
  `_case_0149_date`'s.

## 0150 - Nights looked up by the calendar - done 2026-10-08

What changed: every question about which night is which goes through one
lookup. No rule in `src/core/` asks `MVP_NIGHTS` any more. It is a port: the
same ten nights, the same Endless after them, the same hashes.

**The lookup** (`src/core/waves.gd`):
- `Waves.authored_count()`: how many nights a person wrote, the rows of
  `GameData.NIGHTS`.
- `Waves.plain_night(night, seed)`: the record as written. That is the
  authored row up to `authored_count()`, then `Endless.night` for every day
  of every year.
- `Waves.night_of(night, seed)`: the record the night fights. It is
  `plain_night` plus the calendar's rules, and there are none yet, so it
  hands back the authored row itself. 0152-0154 add their rules there and
  nowhere else.
- Every pure question still goes through `night_of`: `table`, `size_of`,
  `kinds_of`, `spawns_of`, `reward_of`, `summary_of`, `delay_before` and
  `tonight`. `tonight` now passes the run's seed for authored nights too,
  which changes nothing.
- Each counting question now has a form for a record already in hand:
  `size_in`, `kinds_in`, `reward_in`, `spawns_in`. The `_of` forms are those
  over `night_of`.
  - These were not in the prompt. They are how the curve's tests and
    `Endless` read a night as written without copying `Waves`' arithmetic.

**The named questions:**
- `Endless.is_generated` and `step_of` count from `Waves.authored_count()`.
- `Endless._size` takes its base from the last authored night as written:
  `Waves.size_in(Waves.plain_night(authored_count()))`, so a calendar rule
  on that date never moves the curve.
- `Run.final_night()` (new) is the last authored night. `is_over`,
  `is_final_night` and `go_endless` ask it. 0151 makes it the year's last day.
- `Tech.total_available()` and `least_available()` count `Run.final_night()`
  nights: 10 and 40 at best, as before.
- `Rewards.night_step(state)` (new) is where `_lines` and `_money_from` read
  how far the pay has climbed. Today it is `state["night"]`, so nights 1-10
  pay exactly what they did. While in there, the bounty sum is back on
  continued lines; an old edit had flattened it onto one line with tabs in
  the middle.
- `check_nights`' `nights.size() != MVP_NIGHTS` became "at least one written
  night and no more than `Calendar.year_days()`".
- `MVP_NIGHTS` keeps its declaration, now commented as read by no rule and
  deleted by 0151, and its `digest()` line. `grep -rn MVP_NIGHTS src/core`
  finds exactly those two.

**The five rewritten groups** (`src/tools/headless_check.gd`):
- `_task_0059_wave_data`:
  - reads each authored night through `plain_night`;
  - `_ten_of` became `_one_per_night` (one copy per authored night) over a
    new `_copies_of`;
  - `_all_enemies` and `_all_reward` add up the nights as written;
  - "one new thing a night" and "the Giant on the last authored night" read
    `kinds_in(plain_night)`;
  - three asserts are new for the relaxed count: one written night is legal,
    none is refused, a table longer than a year is refused.
- `_task_0060_ten_nights`:
  - the three climbing curves, the gaps, the first-seen table and "the
    night after a new thing" read `plain_night` (`size_in`, `reward_in`,
    `_hit_points_in` - which was `_hit_points_sent`, now over a record -
    and `kinds_in`);
  - the Giant is expected on `Waves.authored_count()`;
  - the nights run start to finish still count against `night_of`, the
    night fought.
- `_task_0061_rewards` gains two asserts:
  - night 9 pays exactly eight steps of `money_per_night` more than night 1
    for the same fight;
  - for every authored night, `night_step` is the night's number and "for
    the night" is `base_money + money_per_night x night`.
- `_task_0062_tech`: the floor and ceiling are a point a night times
  `Run.final_night()`. `_ten_nights` became `_every_night` over
  `Run.final_night()` nights.
- `_task_0070_endless`:
  - the generated records are read with `plain_night` and compared with
    `Endless.night`;
  - its nights are named as steps past `Waves.authored_count()` (11, 12,
    15, ... as before);
  - "it grows" starts from the last authored night as written;
  - the seed asserts compare `size_in` and `kinds_in` of the plain records.

## 0151 - The night is the calendar day - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the night fought at the end of a day is that day's night in the
calendar. Difficulty follows the calendar, a lost night is never fought
again, and the year has 56 nights.

**The rule:**
- `Phases.night_ahead` is `Calendar.date(state)`, so `begin_night` numbers
  the night with the date. It used to be `nights_won + 1`.
- `enter_result` still moves `day` every time and `nights_won` only on a
  win. That is a count now, not an index.
- Losing day 3's night leads to night 4 on day 4. The loss costs that
  night's pay and technology, and a share of the stock.
- `Run.final_night()` is `Calendar.year_days()` (56, Winter 14).
- `Run.is_over` is "the year's last night has been won", read from a fact
  that does not move. The new `Run.beat_the_year` asks
  `Tech.already_paid(state, final_night())`. It never counts wins: a year
  with losses in it still ends on Winter 14 won, and losing Winter 14 is
  not an ending.
- `go_endless` opens on the same fact.
- `Tech.total_available` and `least_available` take an optional night count,
  the run's by default: a year pays 224 at best. `_task_0063_tech_tree`
  keeps "the tree costs more than the best run earns" on the authored ten
  nights, commented that 0220 re-prices the tree against the year.
- `src/app/playtest.gd` says "reached night" from `state.night`.

**The save, version 5** (`State.VERSION`, `Save.migrations()[4]`,
`_night_is_the_date_v4`):
- `day` is kept and is the date.
- `night` is left alone. A night in progress keeps its number until it ends,
  and the calendar takes over at the next `begin_night`.
- `nights_paid` keeps its entries and gains none. A v4 night number is at
  most the nights won, so it is below the day, and no date still ahead can
  already be paid.

## 0152 - Full Moon nights - done 2026-10-08

What changed: days 7 and 14 of every season are Full Moon nights. They bring
a bigger horde, pay double, and are lit so you see further into them. The
day HUD counts down to one.

**The rule:**
- `GameData`:
  - `FULL_MOON_DAYS := [7, 14]`, `FULL_MOON_HORDE_PERCENT := 150` and
    `FULL_MOON_REWARD_PERCENT := 200`, each a `# LEVER`, all three in
    `digest()`'s `calendar` row;
  - `check_calendar` refuses a Full Moon outside the season, and a horde or
    a pay under 100%.
- `Calendar.is_full_moon(date)` and `days_to_full_moon(date)`, which is 0 on
  the night itself, 6 on day 8 and 6 on day 15. Both pure.
- `Waves.night_of` puts the first calendar rule over `plain_night`:
  - every ordinary wave of a Full Moon sends 150% of its count, in integer
    arithmetic and never fewer than written;
  - boss rows are left as written;
  - the record carries `"full_moon": true`, for 0158's forecast;
  - no RNG, so authored and generated nights alike.
  - An ordinary night is still the authored row itself, and the authored
    row is never touched: the Full Moon is a deep copy.
- **A bigger horde still fits the night** (0137). `_fit_inside_the_night`
  shrinks the record's gaps a quarter at a time, then the members' spacing
  through `Endless._fit_before_dawn`; the check is never relaxed. For seed 0:

| Day | Sent | Gap (ticks) | Interval | Sent by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 54 -> 81 | 270, kept | - | 78 s -> 97 s |
| 14 | 125 -> 187 | 120, kept | - | 103 s -> 146 s |
| 21 | 197 -> 293 | 120 -> 0 | - -> 17 | 153 s -> 172 s |
| 28 | 268 -> 399 | 120 -> 0 | 16 -> 12 | 172 s -> 170 s |
| 56 | 554 -> 828 | 120 -> 0 | 6 -> 5 | 163 s -> 163 s |

  The generated Full Moons from day 21 on come as one stream, with no gaps
  between their waves. They are the curve's drafts, and 0270-0274 rewrite
  them; the gaps went first because the prompt orders it. `python
  tools/nights.py --check` still passes on every date of the year, Full
  Moons included.
- **`Waves.tonight` keeps a Full Moon's record** on `wave.tonight` the way it
  keeps a generated night's, and only a record a rule changed. Night 1 is
  still the authored row and puts nothing new in its state.

**The pay** (`Rewards`):
- `moon_percent(state)` is the one place that says what tonight pays of an
  ordinary sum: 200 on a Full Moon, 100 otherwise. 0219 reads it for

- `_lines` and `_money_from` take an optional percent, so the same state
  can be asked under an ordinary sky.
- Money gets a `"full moon"` line: the other lines' total times
  (percent - 100) / 100. Materials are each the percent of their ordinary

- The morning report prints `RES_FULL_MOON` (FULL MOON BONUS / BÔNUS DE LUA
  CHEIA) with the `+$` under "for defending well".

## 0153 - Boss nights repeat until the boss falls - done 2026-10-08

What changed: day 14 of every season is the season's boss night, and the
season does not end until that boss is down. A boss still alive at dawn
walks off with the rest and comes back the next night. There is no loss
penalty, and the farm loses no day of crops or animals.

**The data:**
- `SEASON_BOSSES := [giant, giant, giant, giant]`, one per season, in
  `digest()`'s `calendar` row. 0253-0255 put in their own.
- `check_calendar` requires one boss per season, each an `is_boss` enemy.

**The calendar:**
- `Calendar.is_boss_night(date)` is the season's last day, and
  `Calendar.boss_of(date)` is that season's boss.
- **The hold is a counter, not a frozen day.** A new top-level Phases key,
  `days_held`, grows by one every night a boss night ends without its boss
  down, however it ended. `Calendar.date` is `day - days_held`.
  - `day` still moves every night, so the stall restocks, the report and
    stats count it, and every day system runs.
  - The date stays on 14, so tonight is the boss again.
  - Old saves get 0 from the reconcile; no version bump.

**The night** (`Waves.night_of`, the rule under the Full Moon's):
- A boss date's record has its own bosses taken out and one row of the
  season's boss put in, third from last like `Endless`' Giants, from spawn
  0. It carries `"boss"` for 0158's forecast.
- Every other date loses its `is_boss` rows. Night 10 loses its Giant, and
  `Endless`' every-fifth-night Giants no longer reach the calendar; the
  `giant_every` levers stay for 0279.
- The note says so: "... - and giant, the season's boss" on the boss date,
  "(its boss kept for the season's last night)" where one was removed.
- The Full Moon scales over this and leaves the boss row alone. Spring 14
  is both: 187 ordinary bodies and one Giant.
- `Waves.tonight` keeps any record a rule changed, and `Waves._ruled` says
  which. Night 10 is now one of them.
- `Waves.boss_fell(state)`: every `is_boss` body tonight's record sends has
  been killed, per `killed_by_kind`. True on a night with no boss.
- `Waves.tick` raises `boss_arrived` from `is_boss`. `waves.gd` names no
  enemy any more.

**The third outcome, escaped** (`Sim._test_for_dawn`):
- 0137's interim is gone: dawn no longer waits while `Combat.boss_here`.
- At dawn on a boss night with the boss alive and the house standing,
  `Rewards.settle(state, false, true)` and `Phases.enter_result(state,
  false, true)` record `escaped`:
  - nothing is paid (no money, materials or technology) and nothing taken;
  - `nights_won` stays;
  - no won or lost event (the `dawn` event is there);
  - the payout names the boss;
  - the boss and the survivors walk off in `begin_day` like any morning.
- The house falling is a loss as on any night, and holds the season if the
  boss is alive.
- `nights_paid` is keyed by the date, so a boss night pays its technology
  once, on the night the boss falls.
- The night HUD's countdown comment no longer promises to hold at 0:00.

**The morning report:**
- An escape is headed NIGHT OVER / FIM DA NOITE in the warn colour.
- Its line is `RES_BOSS_ESCAPED` ("GIANT GOT AWAY - IT COMES BACK TONIGHT"
  / "GIGANTE FUGIU - VOLTA HOJE À NOITE", the name through `Names.of`,
  upper-cased), followed by "money and the farm are untouched".
- The line wraps if a boss's name is long: the Scarecrow King will not fit
  one row. Its width column is 0 for that reason.

**What assumed the Giant on night 10:**
- `_task_0003` reads the table as written ("the Giant is written on night
  10").
- `_task_0058_giant` finds it on Spring 14, once in the season's fourteen
  nights.
- 0059/0060 already read `plain_night`.
- 0066's and input_check's 0070 fixtures that win day 56 by fiat put its
  boss down first (`_beat_the_boss`): a boss night is won only once the boss
  fell.
- `perf_check`'s worst case is Spring 14.

**The benchmark: a fix, and a new baseline.**
- On Spring 14, `night_tick` came out at 36 us against the towers' own

## 0154 - The calm night after a boss - done 2026-10-08

What changed: after a boss falls the horde regroups. The first night of the
next season sends nothing, the farmer sleeps through it, and something is
waiting on the porch in the morning. Spring 1 of Year 1 is still the
tutorial's night 1.

**The rule:**
- `Calendar.is_calm(date)` is the first day of a season, except the
  game's first.
  - It is a pure function of the date. That is safe because of 0153's hold:
    the calendar reaches a new season only once its boss is down. So the
    forecast cannot be wrong about it, Spring 1 of Year 2 included.
- `Waves.night_of` returns the calm record before any other rule:
  `{note, opening_ticks: 0, waves: [], calm: true}`.
- `Waves._ruled` includes calm dates, so `tonight()` keeps the record.
- `check_nights` refuses an empty wave list unless the record says calm.
- `Waves.summary_of` prints "night 15  calm  - ...". That line joined
  `headless_check`'s `ALLOWED_IN_RULES` by name, as a developer-facing
  string `tools/nights.py` reads.
- **The night still happens and takes no special road.**
  - The build step opens as on any night.
  - START, or 0128's 30 s after a pass-out, begins it.
  - `Waves.begin` marks an empty table done, and its first tick is
    `_test_for_the_end` with nobody on the farm: won.

**The pay:**
- `CALM_NIGHT_GIFT := {wood: 20, stone: 20, food: 10}`, a `# LEVER`, in
  `digest()` as `calm`.
- `GameData.check_gift` in `validate()` allows known resources only, never
  money or `tech`, never negative.
- `Rewards._lines` returns the gift on a calm night: no night money, no
  materials. `money_from` is empty.
- No technology: `Tech.mark_paid` (new) writes the date into `nights_paid`
  without paying it, so a reload never pays it later either.
- The payout carries `"calm"`.

**On screen:**
- The day HUD's line under the date says CALM NIGHT / NOITE CALMA
  (`DHUD_CALM_TONIGHT`, good face) on a calm date. It outranks dusk and
  the Full Moon's countdown, and gives way to bedtime and the pass-out
  warning.
- The morning report, instead of PAID, has:
  - `RES_CALM_NIGHT`: A CALM NIGHT - THE HORDE REGROUPED / NOITE CALMA - A
    HORDA SE REAGRUPOU, wrapped like 0153's escape line;
  - `RES_GIFT`: A GIFT ON THE PORCH / UM PRESENTE NA VARANDA;
  - the gift itself: +10 food +20 stone +20 wood.

## 0155 - Losing a night when the calendar moves on - done 2026-10-08

What changed: losing costs what the plan says and nothing more. The calendar
moves on, the horde takes a quarter of the stock, it tramples the crops it
walked through, and what it broke stays broken. Only a boss night comes back.

**What was already so, now asserted beside the rest:**
- The calendar moving on after a loss is 0151's rule: a lost night on day 5
  leads to night 6.
- A lost Spring 14 with the boss alive leads to Spring 14 again (0153).
- The stock loss is `Rewards._loss` untouched: 25% of each stock, money
  and technology kept by the `DEFEAT_KEEPS_*` levers.
- A wall destroyed in the night is still gone the next morning: the rubble
  swept, nothing refunded.

**Trampling, new and deterministic:**
- `Pathing.horde_routes(state, regions, reach)` returns the sorted cells
  the horde walked:
  - from every spawn cell of the regions tonight used (`Waves.spawns_in` of
    tonight's record), the flow field's steps (`step_from`) down to the
    house;
  - plus every cell an enemy stands on when it is asked;
  - widened by `reach` tiles each way.
  - It uses no randomness: two copies of a state trample the same cells.
- `TRAMPLE_REACH := 0` (`# LEVER`, 0-2) is in `digest()`'s `defeat` row,
  and `validate()` refuses it outside 0-2.
- `Farming.trample(state, cells)`:
  - a plot on the cells with a crop keeps its tilled ground and loses its
    crop, growth and soak;
  - it gets a `trampled` marker naming the crop, which `_plant` erases;
  - `Farming` sees empty tilled ground.
  - No migration: a missing marker means nothing was trampled.
- `Rewards.settle` tramples in its loss branch, after the stock is taken,
  and the payout's `trampled` says how many. A won night, an escape or a
  calm night tramples nothing.
- **On today's farm the routes cross no soil.** The fields lie west and
  south of the house and the horde comes from the east, so for now this
  hits crops only where somebody planted on the path. 0167 makes any grass
  tillable, and then it will matter.

**On screen:**
- The morning report has `RES_TRAMPLED` / `.other` (%d CROP(S) TRAMPLED /
  %d PLANTA(S) PISOTEADA(S)), in the bad colour, under "came down". The
  bare key is the singular, as `I18n.plural` reads the table, not `.one`.
- The trampled plot is drawn through 0120's road. `PlaceholderArt.ART`
  gains `trampled` (pack A014, `res://sprites/crops/trampled.png`, 16x16
  at (8,14), drawn by code), and `WorldView._trampled_sprite` draws it
  until A014 is integrated by 0197.
- **The stand-in is the crop's ripe frame, not its first stage**, pressed
  to half height at its foot and darkened (`TRAMPLED_TINT`). This departs
  from the prompt's suggestion, tried first: carrot's first stage is a
  three-pixel sprout, and flattened it is a dash that reads as bare earth.
  The ripe frame flattened reads as a plant somebody walked on.
- **Text that still said the same night comes back:** `run.gd`'s header now
  says the calendar moves on and only a boss night returns, and a
  `state.gd` comment said "until the same night came back". `phases.gd` had
  already been rewritten in 0151. No tutorial or report text said it.
  `_task_0065` is 0151's and was not touched.

**Tests:** `_task_0155_losing` (headless_v1):
- a lost night on day 5, confirmed, then the road to the next night: night
  6;
- a lost Spring 14 with the boss alive: date 14 again;
- every stock against `DEFEAT_LOSS_PERCENT`, money, technology and energy

- on a farm with carrots on every cell of the east route and every cell
  beside it, the route worked out in the test down the flow field from

- a trampled plot is empty tilled ground;
- two copies lose and trample the same cells;
- a won night tramples nothing;

- `TRAMPLE_REACH` is inside 0-2.

  south `(35-44, 55)`. They are 0156's `SPAWN_BANDS`, cell for cell, ten each.
  Indices 0 and 1 did not move.
- `SPAWN_SIDES`: `east`, `south_east`, `north`, `west`, `south`, the
  forecast's words, in `SPAWNS` order.

## 0158 - The forecast - done 2026-10-08

What changed: from 18:00, and in the build step, a panel at the top right
says what tonight sends:
- the sides in words;
- the waves;
- a Full Moon, a boss or a calm night;
- one head and count per kind.

It is built from the record the night will fight, so it cannot be wrong.
The night HUD's strip now names the date beside the night, through the
waves too.

**The rules** (`src/core/forecast.gd`, `class_name Forecast`):
- `Forecast.of(seed, date)` returns `{date, season, day_of_season,
  full_moon, boss, calm, sides, waves, kinds, count, event}`.
  - It reads only `Waves.night_of(date, seed)`, with its flags, and
    `Calendar`.
  - `sides` are `SPAWN_SIDES` ids in `SPAWNS` order.
  - `kinds` are `[kind, count]` pairs in the order each kind first arrives,
    an Array rather than a Dictionary, so nothing iterates an unordered one.
  - `event` is `&""`, for 0256.
- `Forecast.tonight(state)` asks for `Calendar.date(state)`, the night the
  build step opens on.
- It reads `state["seed"]` and never `state["rng"]`. Nothing in it is random
  yet, so it opens no stream; 0256's events will open a `(seed, date)` one
  as `Endless._stream_for` does.

**The panel** (`src/ui/forecast_panel.gd`, built by `Main` after the night
HUD, under every panel):
- Up by day from `Phases.is_dusk` and in the build step. Down at noon, once
  the waves start, inside the house (where the day HUD is down too) and

## 0159 - Seasons on screen - done 2026-10-08

What changed: the same farm through the year, all of it in the view:
- spring is today's art;
- summer is warmer;
- autumn is ochre and rust;
- winter is snow, with snowfall and snow on the roofs.

Not one rule changed, and the night ramp still lies over every season.

**The tables** (`tools/palette.py`, written into `PaletteData` by
`tools/gen_sprites.py`, whose `palette_gd()` now also writes `FOLIAGE` and
`SEASON_REMAP`):
- `FOLIAGE`: the grass and leaf ramps, plus `rot_dark` and `rot`, because
  the terrain draws its darkest grass tufts in them.
- Each season maps those entries onto other palette entries:
  - summer moves each green a step towards the sun, and the brightest goes
    to `gold_light`;
  - autumn sends the grass to the wood and gold ramps and the leaves to roof
    rust;
  - winter sends both to `bone`, `bone_dark`, `moon` and `stone_light`.
- No new `COLOURS` entry.

**The remap:**
- `src/ui/season.gdshaderinc` is shared by the new
  `src/ui/season_remap.gdshader` and by `ambient_motion.gdshader`. A tree
  can wear only one material, and its own is the wind.
- `season_remap` goes on the terrain, edge and corner layers (one material,
  `SeasonView.ground`), the roofs and the cap stand-ins.
- Every texel is remapped by exact palette match. In the tree's crown that
  happens before the wind's subpixel blend, so a leaf mid-sway is still a
  remapped leaf.
- **The terrain is never redrawn for a season.** Switching is the `season`
  uniform. `WorldView.terrain_draws()` counts the cell lays, and the input
  case asserts it does not move.
- The art is imported lossless (`compress/mode=0`), so an exact match is
  exact.

**`SeasonView`** (`src/ui/season_view.gd`, a node under `WorldView`):
- **When the season changes:** `season_on_screen(state)` is the date's
  season, except under the morning report, where it stays the season of the
  night just fought. The date moves at dawn (`enter_result`), so the farm
  turns on the season's first morning, behind 0138's wake-up, and every
  material switches in the same frame.
- **The hooks for 0163 and 0164:**
  - `frame_for(name, season)` gives `<name>_<season>` when 0120's lookup
    has it, and the base name otherwise.
  - `carries_season` and `stand_in` tell real seasonal art from a stand-in.
    Real art gets no remap; a registered stand-in still does.
  - `_apply_ground_art` puts a seasonal terrain atlas on the tile set when
    one exists.
  - Plots ask for `crops/tilled_<season>`.
  - Trees ask for `props/tree_<season>`.
  - Nodes ask for `cap_for`: `props/<art>_snow`, `snow_cap` or
    `snow_cap_2x2`.
- **The registry:** 27 new `ART` entries.
  - A012 (12): `atlas_winter`, the nine winter tiles and the two winter
    plots.
  - A013 (15): the six seasonal trees, seven own caps and the two generic
    caps.
  - Each resolves to its base frame. `tools/placeholders.py` lists both
    packs (107 stand-ins over 15 packs) until 0163 and 0164 delete them.

**Winter's extras:**
- **Snowfall** (`Particles`):
  - 40 flakes a second over the camera's view, in `bone` and `moon`, from
    the same ring as every particle, so `video/max_particles` still caps it;
  - scaled by `a11y/particle_density` (none at 0), and off when particles
    do not move;
  - the first snowy frame fills the whole view, so winter does not open on
    an empty sky.
- **Snow on the roofs, by a code mask:** the top rows of the house's, the
  stall's and the stations' opaque pixels (the whole drawing, or its top
  quarters).
  - Three tries, by the shots:
    1. Snow in place of the outline melted into the snowy field.
    2. Snow under the art's own line left the line's gappy pixels floating
       over it as dots - a dotted halo round the house and the workshop.
    3. What shipped: each column's top pixel is an unbroken line (the art's
       when it drew one, `ink` where it left a gap) and the two rows under
       it are snow.
  - It reads as snow on the stall's awning. On the house and the workshop
    it reads as a snowy rim rather than a roof under snow.
  - **Proposed pack:** winter roofs for the house, the workshop, the stall
    and the stations, drawn rather than masked.
- **Snow caps' stand-in:** the host's own frame through the same mask,
  snow only, so it sits exactly on the host. At a rock's 16 px it is a
  line and two rows; A013's caps are the real thing.

**A finding for whoever writes the next shader:** the first verify passed
every check in the art showcases, but each still printed
`Condition "!actions.custom_samplers.has(...)" is true` and so failed.
- The cause: Godot 4.7's canvas shader compiler logs that error when a
  built-in `TEXTURE` is handed to a function as a `sampler2D` argument.
- The include's helpers now take no sampler. The snow's sampling loop
  lives in `season_remap.gdshader`'s own `fragment()`.

**Deviations and notes:**
- **Trees: A013 and this prompt disagree.** A013 asks for spring blossom
  and today's green in summer. This prompt makes spring today's art and
  summer warmer. I followed the prompt, so summer's trees are warmed too.
  0164 decides; turning the summer remap off for trees is one line in
  `_refresh`.
- Crops on the plots keep their green all year. Seasonal crops are a later
  task's.
- Against `docs/reference-sheet.png`: the sheet's day ground is a golden
  green, closer to this summer than to today's spring. Spring stays today's
  art, as the prompt says.

**The check that a table maps everything** (`_task_0159_palette`,
headless_v1):
- It reads every PNG in `sprites/terrain/` and both trees, and collects the
  `FOLIAGE` colours they use.
- `SeasonView.unmapped` must find nothing in any season.
- A scratch autumn without `grass` must be caught (`["autumn: grass"]`).
- Every target is a palette entry, spring is the identity, and winter's
  targets are the pale four.
- **Tried, reverted:** I took `rot` out of autumn in `tools/palette.py` and
  regenerated. The group failed with `["autumn: rot"]`. Restored, then
  `gen_sprites.py --check` was OK.
- It also asserts the season on screen (under Spring 14's report it is
  still spring) and the lookups.

**Tests:**
- `_case_0159_seasons` (input_v1): the remap reads 0, 1, 2, 3 for Spring,
  Summer, Autumn and Winter 3. It snows on Winter 3 and not in spring.
  Zero density stops it. The terrain was laid no more times. Spring of
  Year 2 is spring again.
- The shot scenario count is 41.

**Shots** (`implementation/shots/0159/`, FHD, opened):
- `noon`: unchanged, spring.
- `season_summer`: brighter yellow-green grass, gold in the crowns.
- `season_autumn`: an ochre field, rust and gold trees. The path still reads,

- `season_winter`: a snow field, snowy trees, falling snow, snow under a
  line on the stall's awning and the roof rims. The paths and the beds
  read brown through it.
- `season_winter_night`: the same under the night ramp: blue-violet snow,
  the windows the warm things.
- `winter_build`: 0157's scenario, now in winter at night.

## 0165 - Crops grow by days - done 2026-10-09

Crops now advance once each morning if watered the previous day: carrot in
3 days, wheat in 4 and corn in 8. Dry plots wait without losing progress.
Bedtime records a pending credit before drying the field; morning consumes it,
including after passing out and after a boss holds the calendar. Trampling
and harvesting clear any pending credit. The old per-tick growth and soak
bank are gone, and Farming is no longer a per-tick benchmark system.

The seed strip, shop and tooltip use days and whole harvests per fourteen-day
season in English and pt_BR. The helpers are now days_to_grow,
harvests_per_season and value_per_season. The autoplayer refills its can and
keeps a carrot/corn field plan instead of relying on unwatered crops growing
while it gathers. The crop-ready music note now announces morning harvest
news anywhere on the farm, including while the farmer wakes indoors.

Save version 7 migrates legacy tick growth proportionally to whole days,
rounding down while keeping ready crops ready, and removes soak. The migration
uses fixed legacy durations. Three new run-v7 goldens were written through
make_goldens.gd; no older golden was overwritten. Tests cover delayed dry
carrots, readiness on the third watered morning, credit consumed once,
bed/pass-out on a held boss date, a half-grown legacy golden, rounding,
ready preservation and a pending credit across save/reload. Historical tests,
art fixtures, the house migration check and screenshot ages use the new units.

## 0166 - A day of eight to ten minutes - done 2026-10-09

The day now lasts 16,800 ticks: 560 seconds, or 9 minutes 20 seconds.
The 06:00-02:00 clock gets 14 ticks per minute, and derived dusk remains
18:00 at tick 10,080. Core/UI searches found no SECONDS-based day_tick hour
thresholds; bedtime reminders and pass-out continue through the clock helpers.

Production arithmetic: 16,800 / 7,200 = 7/3. Recipe periods are the old
seconds times DAY_TICKS/240: barricade/fence/mine/wall 420/350/560/700 ticks,
corn/fish oil 1400/1750, incendiary/gunpowder 700/1050, and meal/fish/roast
840/1050/1260. Nominal full-power daily output stays 40/48/30/24 kits,
12/9 oil, 96/32 ammunition and 40/48/52 food. Continuous queues need inputs;
a fresh day loses the final production tick to pass-out and can deliver one
batch fewer where the interval divides the day exactly. Tech and brownouts
still modify actual crafting time.

Trees and ore regrow in DAY_TICKS/2 = 8400 ticks (280 seconds), retaining two
harvests per initial node including swing time. Seams use 3*DAY_TICKS/8 =
6300 (210 seconds), retaining three. Boulders remain permanent clearances.
The event-based cliff fixture measures 16 iron on a tight route, 16 with
45-tick walks and 13 with deliberately poor DAY_TICKS/18 walks. A ten-second
walk no longer consumes enough of the larger day to be the bad-route case.
Cows use DAY_TICKS/3 = 5600, chickens 5*DAY_TICKS/24 = 3500; before pass-out,
prompt collection permits 2/4 meat respectively, with the unchanged 2/1 caps.
Fishing waits 140-700 ticks, averaging 420: forty mean waits per nominal day,
before reaction/travel. Its 45-tick human reaction window stays unchanged.
A loaded generator spends four oil per day at DAY_TICKS/4 = 4200 ticks each;
the global period also lasts 140 seconds at night, intentionally up from 60.
Shop quantities stay wood 15, stone 12, iron 8, wheat 10, corn 8, carrot 12:
they already restock once per day and must not scale with real-time length.
BALANCE.md records these capacities and their assumptions.

Clock suites now rig the tick just before each boundary, then use Sim.advance
for the actual transition. Regrowth and mining fixtures jump between real
expiry/strike events; livestock, power and idle queues rig their countdowns
and exercise actual completion ticks. Short seeded replays use 600 ticks;
the standalone determinism scenario retains its full length. The defeat
fixture's existing 900 daytime ticks were already bounded. The title starts
its disposable backdrop at the opening clock instead of simulating a day
on each visit; its input case and both v1 suites retain their coverage.
Autoplay suite policies sleep at 20:00, early enough to fit the budget but
late enough to mine the second ore harvest needed for the first tower.
The initial 10:00 fixture correctly failed to fund a tower and was corrected.

The standalone robot still works until 01:30. Its old fixed 900-action guard
truncated the new day; the guard now follows the tick budget. A short
`python tools/autoplay.py 4 --nights=1` took 17.6 seconds: all four seed-9000
policies played 16,381 day ticks, then cleared the first night with 10 house HP.
Each earned $0 cash and spent $24 before the night reward (net -$24).
They do not sell their gathered materials, so unsold value is not counted
as cash income. The short-run report now exposes both cash figures and ticks.
The balance reader parsed the actual report into four winning policies;
all seven lever patterns matched once. Its stale brownout regex, fixed to
25 despite today's 50, now accepts the current number. A full multi-lever,
ten-night balance sweep was not rerun for this duration change.

Saved day_tick values remain ticks since 06:00; for example 4200 now reads
11:00 instead of 17:40. Existing producer countdowns retain their remaining
ticks and use the new period on the next cycle. State.VERSION stays 7 and
no migration or new golden is required.
