What changed: the hoe turns empty grass into a plot, and planting, watering
and harvesting use the same rules as the starter beds. Terrain bytes stay
unchanged. Bare grass takes the hoe only in front of the farmer, never as
an underfoot fallback, including at the farm boundary; existing plots retain
underfoot planting, watering and harvesting. Occupied and non-farm ground
refuse the hoe.

Empty grass plots return to lawn after TILLED_GRASS_FADES_DAYS=3 mornings;
planted grass and starter soil never fade. Successful work records
last_worked_morning only on grass, preserving soil plot shapes and save
version 7. The absolute day counter counts mornings even when a boss holds
the calendar. Legacy grass plots acquire their missing age on the first
loaded morning. Harvesting and trampling renew the empty ground's grace
period; unsuccessful actions do not.

Farming.field_cells supplies starter soil plus tilled grass in index order
to the tutorial, autoplay and all field fixtures. Autoplay keeps its terrain
scan cached while incorporating new/faded grass. Title and shot backdrops sow
the starter field rather than every newly actionable lawn tile. The ordinary
soil-only field retains its existing order without an extra sort, avoiding
a measured tutorial performance regression.

Path cost: tilled grass keeps the grass cost. Hoeing does not call Farm.touch
or invalidate any flow field, so each stroke avoids a roughly 9 ms route
rebuild. Turf borders use N1/E2/S4/W8 side masks and NW/NE/SE/SW concave caps;
starter soil and neighbouring plots join without an internal grass seam.
The placeholder road reuses the existing terrain edge textures over today's
dry/wet earth. The final A014 geometry is 16x16, pivot (8,16), draw scale 1.0,
with clockwise runtime quarter-turns and the grass season-remap material.
A014 now names 0171 as the withered-crop owner.

## 0169 - An inventory for many things - done 2026-10-09

What changed: the ledger now shows one category at a time, with translated
vertical tabs and bounded pages. Materials, crops, seeds, fish, animal goods,
artisan goods, ammunition, night leftovers and the farm follow the 1.0 plan;
empty categories have no tab. The twelve crops take two pages, and all 24
current resources appear once across eight pages. ROW_HEIGHT is 16 pixels and
ROW_SPACE is 160, giving ten rows per page; a seventy-row fixture retains all
items in seven slices without increasing the frame.

Navigation reuses InputActions' hotbar_prev / hotbar_next: Q/E on the keyboard,
LB/RB on a pad, with the saved bindings shown on the arrows. These actions turn
inventory pages while the ledger is open and select defences when it is closed.
Mouse arrows visit every page; a category tab opens its first page. Paging is
view state only, wraps at either end, and leaves the simulation untouched. The
early page handler also forwards the event to Actions' device tracker so the
arrow labels follow the device in hand. The clock continues behind the ledger.

The HUD keeps two rows of three: wood, stone, iron; food, money, tech (the plan's
essence). Materials pay for defences, food repairs them, money buys seeds and
defences, and essence funds lasting upgrades. Oil and wheat remain in their
inventory categories. The existing purse stays in place; its refresh cache is
separate from the resource-grid cache so both money displays update together.

GameData.validate now rejects an ungrouped resource by name, including an entry
in GROUP_OTHER, and rejects a resource without SELL_PRICE, except money, energy
and tech. Headless checks require every resource's literal Names.KEYS / ITEM_*
entry in English and Portuguese. Category names have a separate literal key
table. UiKit's resource icon lookup falls back through the placeholder road to
existing approved wood art if the item's own icon has not arrived; the missing
art diagnostic still reports missing dedicated icons. No art PNG was generated,
drawn or edited. The later fish-species prompt now names the fish group rather
than the retired larder group.

## 0170 - Crops keep to their seasons - done 2026-10-09

What changed: each crop has its plan sowing season. The strip and its six
number keys offer only today's crops, show held packet counts, and select the
first available crop when the previous choice leaves season; winter has no
selection. Sowing spends one packet and no money. Twelve named, translated,
priced packet resources join the seeds category and the flat daily shelf.
The shop's extra seed rows remain an in-season picker, with held quantities;
actual purchases use the ordinary buy rows. Tutorial and crop descriptions
now explain packets, and long shop labels wrap without stretching buttons.

Price decision: packet purchases use a Shop.buy_price branch reading the
crop's seed_cost, which is also the cost used by check_crops. Carrot costs $2
and resells for $1: its old $1 purchase could not lose money on resale while
0169 requires every tangible item's positive sale price. Other purchase
costs remain wheat $2, garlic $3, corn/potato $4, pepper $5, sunflower $6,
beet $7, strawberry $8, grape $9, melon $10 and pumpkin $11. Packet resale
prices are $1/$2/$3/$4 and every purchase loses on selling back.
Dominance is compared only between crops sharing a sowing season, since the
original carrot/corn/wheat trio no longer offers simultaneous choices.
All twelve packet shelves carry 20 per day all year; seasonal stock remains
0190's. New farms get six carrot, two potato and two garlic packets.

Save decision: State.VERSION remains 7. Missing packet balances in old held
and gained tables reconcile to zero, not the starter gift. New shelves are
added to old saves without refilling already exhausted shelves, so an old
save can immediately buy packets. The pure selection getter never writes
state; dawn, sowing and reconciliation persist its fallback through core.
Planted crops still follow the existing watered-morning rules, including
across season changes; field expiry and winter behavior remain 0171's.

Fixtures: SuiteKit.crop_supplies gives test/tool farms packets and a valid
crop date. Explicit wheat/corn, round-robin fields, determinism, golden maker,
perf and shot fixtures use it. The disposable title backdrop is always spring
and supplies its own packets through Resources.add: src/tools is excluded
from shipped exports, so production UI cannot depend on SuiteKit. The robot
buys packets at the stall and chooses carrot, corn or wheat in their season;
it skips sowing in winter. The shared input harness scrolls controls into
view before clicking. New 0170 rule/input cases cover packet consumption,
missing packets, off-season refusal, summer/winter choices, dawn fallback,
old-save purchases and buying/picking/sowing potato through real input.

belong to it. Winter 1 withers everything autumn left in the ground: plots
stay tilled, lose growth and watering credit, and retain a withered marker
until replanted. A crop sown for the new season that morning survives.

cannot begin sowing, and the highlighted bed explains why. The winter seed
strip says nothing grows outside, wrapped into the empty rows.
Fishing, mining and seam regrowth, a two-job press queue and cow production
are covered by direct winter checks; their existing rules are unchanged.

## 0172 - Crops that grow back - done 2026-10-09

What changed: strawberry and corn regrow after four watered mornings; pepper
and grape after three. Picking leaves the plant in its own regrowth stage,
short of the existing growth threshold, and consumes no new packet. Watered
mornings still go through Phases.begin_day; dry mornings wait, and the first
morning of the next season withers regrowing plants as well. The existing
REMOVE action clears the faced plant with the hoe (right mouse / right-stick
press), without another payout; its localized highlight explains the action.
Only unhandled input reaches the hoe, so menu clicks stay in their menus.

The optional plot marker defaults to false. Growth still counts watered
mornings toward the original threshold; State.VERSION remains 7, and both
old plots and new regrowth saves are covered. A015/A016/A017 placeholders use
existing stage-2 crop textures with a separate regrowth tint and the packs'
final geometry; no PNG art was generated, drawn or edited.

Balance: value_per_day had already become value_per_season in 0170. That
current helper and check_crops now share the whole-harvest calculation:
1 + floor((14 - initial_growth) / regrow_days) for regrowing crops, with one
seed cost for the plant; single-harvest crops retain floor(14 / growth) and
a seed cost per harvest. This keeps the existing 14-watered-morning season
estimate. The table shows why no crop dominates another in its season on all
three axes: net value, harvesting visits, and initial packet capital.

## 0173 - Five tools, three tiers - done 2026-10-09

What changed: five permanent tools now have a saved three-step ladder. The
workshop sells iron hoe/can/axe/pickaxe and fibre/iron rods for money and iron,
finishes each order into a pending delivery, and hands it over next morning.
The old tool remains usable; owned tools and pending deliveries survive the
25% stock loss. Orders refuse duplicates and skipped tiers. Gold stays listed
with an unavailable-ore reason until 0176 supplies its costs.

The workshop has localized craft/tools tabs, reasons and a pending marker;
the inventory has a separate page for the five tools without stock counts or
sale values. Both draw A019 through the 0120 placeholder registry (30 native
icon/HUD bindings, no generated or edited PNG art). PlayerWork maps the three
fixed steel head colours to the held tier through a cached view-only shader,

## 0174 - The can and the hoe by tier - done 2026-10-09

What changed: basic, iron and gold cans/hoes now affect one, three and five
cells across the farmer's facing. Farming.action_cells is the shared, read-only
footprint: it visits the centre, the farmer's left, right, then the outer left
and right. The can skips wet, ripe, unplanted or occupied cells and spends one
unit per eligible plot, stopping when empty. One timed hoe action turns its
whole eligible strip, skipping paths, water, rock, buildings and existing plots.
The deliberate REMOVE action from 0172 still clears only the selected crop.

Shape, facing north (numbers are spending/working order):

```text
Gold:  [4] [2] [1] [3] [5]
Iron:      [2] [1] [3]
Basic:         [1]
                ^
              farmer
```

The strip rotates with the four facings and clips at the map boundary. There
is no charge-up or extra hoe time. TOOL_AREA_OFFSETS carries the geometry/order
in GameData with LEVER comments, validation and digest coverage; duplicate or
out-of-width offsets are rejected. The tier areas and capacity bonuses were
already declared by 0173. Activating bonuses 0/4/8 makes capacity 8/12/16, or
10/14/18 with full cans (+2). Refilling uses that capacity; the HUD finally
prints Farming.can_capacity rather than the fixed base 8.

fixture shows a cleared garden so trees do not obscure the three frames or the
farmer. No PNG art was generated, drawn or edited.

## 2026-10-09 — Follow-up: review of Codex's 0160-0176

Codex ran the loop for 0160 and 0165-0176: thirteen tasks. 0161-0164 wait
for art. The review covered three things:
- every commit, read against its prompt's "Done when" and the house rules;
- the full verify on Codex's head: 59 passed, and perf failed alone, then
  passed run by itself on a quiet machine;
- the shots, opened.

All thirteen are done, and both hash chains are continuous and journaled.
These were wrong, and are fixed here.

**0172 - SPACE lost the bed underfoot.** This was the serious one.
- To let REMOVE reach a faced crop, `Player.target` pointed at any faced crop.
- So a farmer standing on an empty bed, facing a watered crop, pressed SPACE
  and nothing happened.
- Fix: `Player.target` is reverted, and REMOVE asks its own
  `Player.clear_target`, which reaches the same cells it reached before.

**0172 - REMOVE could sell a building.**
- A REMOVE outside build mode that cleared nothing stayed in the intent.
- It then fell through to `Building.tick`, which by day sells whatever stands
  on the last cell the build cursor pointed at.
- Fix: it is now spent either way.

**0172 with 0171 - the season's harvest estimate counted 14 mornings.**
- A crop sown on a season's first day is credited on the mornings of days 2
  to 14. The next season's first morning withers it before its credit.
- `crop_harvests` now counts those 13 mornings. In the seed list's
  "/season" column:
  - pepper goes from 4 harvests to 3;
  - grape from 3 to 2 ($123 to $79);
  - sunflower from 2 to 1.
- A new check plays a watered season for every crop and compares the
  harvests with the estimate. `check_crops` still finds no dominant crop.

**0173 - the workshop's upgrade rows chose the bench's recipe.**
- Focusing or clicking one wrote `selected_recipe`, so SPACE at the bench then
  ordered that upgrade. Once ordered it was refused, so SPACE did nothing at
  the bench.
- The rows now only queue. Like the inventory's buttons, they take no
  keyboard focus: a clicked row kept the focus and took the next SPACE or
  Enter as its own press too, which queued twice.

**0173 - its keyboard path was not real.**
- `_case_0173_upgrade` focused the row from code before pressing Enter.
  Nothing a player can press reaches that list.
- Both orders in the case are now the mouse's. The keyboard and pad path is a
  question for the owner (below).

**0167 - a green seam between the starter beds and hoed lawn.**
- The beds' terrain edges are laid once, and they drew grass toward a lawn
  the hoe had turned.
- `_edge_tile` and `_corner_mask` now take the turned cells.
- `_relay_edges_for_turned` lays the edges again around a plot that comes or
  goes.
- The terrain itself is still never laid again: `terrain_draws` is unchanged,
  and that is asserted.

**0160 - the year's ending** read "57 days lived, 56 nights won", because the
date had moved at dawn. It also listed defences without plurals ("4 besta
automática, 13 cerca").
- It now reads 56 days.
- `RES_COUNTED` is "%s x%d", like the shop's rows.

**Shots:**
- Every winter scenario since 0170 divided by zero in `_a_sown_field`,
  because winter has no seeds. Winter beds are now turned and left bare.
- `till_grass` sowed wheat, an autumn crop since 0170, and its packets moved
  the fixture to Autumn 1. It now sows carrot and potato and is back on
  Spring 2.

**Strings:** `WHY_GATHER_SEASON` in pt_BR now reads "Disponível a partir de
%s" ("available from"). It used to say "desde" ("since").

**Not changed - questions for the owner:**
- **Generator fuel at night (0166).** The fuel period is now `DAY_TICKS / 4`,
  which is 140 s at night too, where it used to be 60 s. Night power costs
  half the oil.
  - The journal calls this intentional, without saying why.
  - `_task_0033_power` sets the countdown back to 60 s, so the test never sees

- **REMOVE on crops (0172).** A right click clears any crop, ripe ones

- **Credits (0160).** They say "Art from approved Codex packs".
- **Money in the HUD (0169).** It shows twice, as "$ 674" and "money 674".

- the winter seed strip keeps its column header above the message;

## 0177 - Hardwood - done 2026-10-09

What changed: the four big stumps 0156 laid in the south-west woods now give
**hardwood**, and only to an iron axe. This is a reason to buy the iron axe
early. Each stump is one thing over 2x2 cells:
- a swing at any of its four cells strikes it;
- it is drawn chipped from the first swing until the last;
- the last swing takes all four cells off the farm;
- it comes back whole the next day.

Hardwood only sells for now; the strong wall of 0231 is what it is for.

**The levers** (`GameData.GATHERING["hardwood_stump"]`):
- axe, `min_tier` 1;
- 6 swings, where a tree takes 3;
- 2 s a swing at tier 0, which is 40 ticks with the iron axe;
- 2 hardwood;
- `regrow_ticks` = `DAY_TICKS`.

`SELL_PRICE[HARDWOOD]` is 6, in the materials group right after wood. With
the iron axe a stump is 8 s of swinging for $12, about half a tree's money
per second ($3/s). Its worth is meant to be the wall's, not the stall's.

**One thing over four cells** (`Gathering`):
- `strike` and `swings_left` resolve the cell to its anchor (`Building.anchor_of`).
  The swing count lives on the anchor's occupant, so all four cells answer
  the same.
- The last swing removes every cell of `Building.footprint` and schedules one
  `regrowing` entry: the anchor's.
- `tick` brings a footprint back only when all of its cells are clear. Each
  restored cell carries the anchor, as `Farm.initial()` lays the map's.
- If the player has built on one cell, the stump **waits**: its entry stays
  pending and is asked again every tick. A tree on a built cell is given up;
  a stump is not, so nothing is spent for good.
- `tick` now clamps a pending count at 0, so a waiting entry does not run
  negative in the save. A one-cell entry leaves the list the tick it reaches
  0, so nothing else changes.

**Other pieces:**
- `Interact.OCCUPANT_VERBS` gives the stump `chop`.
- The tier gate is 0175's, per cell. A basic axe sees "Needs iron axe" in
  both languages, and the input case reads it on the highlight.
- The flow field already treated a node with no `Building` entry as a tree
  (`Pathing._through` returns `IMPASSABLE`, and the stump is not prey). Now
  it is asserted.
- `check_reachable` already walked the stumps through `UNGATHERED_NODES`.
  That list stays, because the v5-to-v6 save migration lays its nodes into
  an old farm. Its comment no longer calls them inert.

**The view:**
- `WorldView.struck_art` draws `<id>_chipped` from the first swing to the
  last, whenever the registry names that state.
- The stand-in `hardwood_stump_chipped` (A021) is 0156's 2x stump tinted paler
  and warmer: fresh wood against the whole stump's darker bark. Side by side
  it reads; it is only a tint until A021's notch arrives in 0204.
- Hardwood's icons, `icon_hardwood` and `hud_hardwood` (A020, integrated by
  0203), are tinted stand-ins of the wood icons, in A020's darker reddish
  heartwood.
- A021's Deliverables now state the settled geometry: six 16x16 nodes at
  (8,14); the stump 32x32 at (16,30) on the bottom centre of its 2x2, in two
  states (whole, then chipped from the first swing until it falls).

**Tests:**
- `_task_0177_hardwood` (headless_v1):
  - the levers and the materials group;
  - the name in both languages;
  - a basic axe refused, with the state hash unchanged;
  - six iron swings across all four cells counting down on one stump;
  - the yield;
  - all four cells empty with exactly the anchor's entry pending;
  - back whole and anchored after `regrow_ticks`;
  - a fence on one cell keeps all four empty, and the stump survives a save
    while waiting;
  - back the tick the fence goes;
  - `check_reachable`;
  - the flow field's treatment, the same as a tree's.
- `_case_0177_hardwood` (input_v1), with real SPACE beside a non-anchor cell:
  - refused with a basic axe, and the highlight names the iron axe;
  - with the iron axe, the first swing draws it chipped;
  - held SPACE fells all four cells;
  - the hardwood arrives once.
- Shot count 61 in `headless_check`, which asks for one per scenario.

**Notes:**
- The 2x2 stand-in fills only the bottom row of its footprint, as A021's
  envelope asks ("broad, not tall"). So the highlight on a top cell frames
  grass above the stump. It still says chop; a footprint-wide highlight
  would be a view task of its own.
- The `hardwood` scenario stands him north of the chipped stump. The seed
  list has covered the left of the screen since 0168, and the whole stump
  further east stays in the same frame.

### Hashes

Both moved on purpose, accepted with `verify.py --accept`.
- **SIM 265134837 -> 3052463561**: `hardwood` is a new key in `held` and

- **DATA 1698799174 -> 2340660337**: the stump's `GATHERING` row,

## 0178 - Sprinklers - done 2026-10-09

What changed: copper, iron and gold sprinklers. They are built by day from
the build list on one cell. Every morning, after the growth credit, each one
waters the plots of its pattern for the new day, so a big field stops costing
the whole morning. At night zombies walk over them; they are never a wall.

**Decided: three ids, not one with levels.** `copper_sprinkler`,
`iron_sprinkler` and `gold_sprinkler` are `BUILDINGS` entries:
- **Costs:** $50 + 3 copper, $120 + 6 iron, $250 + 4 gold. Each is paid
  directly, in its own metal and money, so there is no recipe, no new
  station in `selected_recipe`, and no change to the state's shape.
- hp 30/40/50, 1x1, no energy.
- These are A018's own row names, so the pack needs no rename.
- Each entry declares its pattern as levers: `spray` (`cross` or `square`)
  and `spray_reach`.
  - copper is a cross of reach 1: the four beside it;
  - iron is a square of 1: the 3x3;
  - gold is a square of 2: the 5x5.

**The morning** (`Farming.sprinkle`, called from `Phases.begin_day` right after
`Farming.morning`):
- Every sprinkler, in sorted cell order, marks its pattern's plots
  (`Farming.sprayed_by`, in index order, never off the farm) watered for the
  new day.
- Tonight's dry-out turns that into tomorrow's growth, like any watering.
- Turned earth with nothing in it is wetted too, so a seed sown there later
  that day grows. The spray is not the farmer working the bed, so turned lawn
  still fades by 0167's rule.

**Never a wall.** `Building.walked_over(id)` reads the entries' declared
`walked_over` flag:
- `Pathing._through` prices the cell at its ground, the way it prices a trap;
- `is_prey` does not count it, so no breaker hunts it;
- `breaks_through` does not count it, so a zombie walks over it rather than
  biting.

The farmer walks round one, as round anything built (`Farm.walkable`).

**A cell with a sprinkler is not a plot:**
- `Building.why_not` refuses one on a crop, with `WHY_ON_A_CROP`;
- put down on turned earth, it erases that plot;
- tilling and planting already skip an occupied cell.

`check_buildings` refuses each of these, and `SPRAY_SHAPES` is in `digest()`:
- an unknown spray shape;
- a reach outside 1-3;
- a sprinkler that is not one walked-over cell.

**The view:**
- **The body:** through the placeholder road until A018 is integrated by
  0201. The stand-in is the spent mine's low metal disc, tinted copper, iron
  or gold and scaled to A018's widths (8, 10 and 12 px), so the tiers differ
  in size as well as colour.
- **The spray** is code particles (`Particles._spray`), from 06:00 to 07:00
  for every sprinkler in view:
  - drops fly out along the four ways for a cross and all round for a square,
    further with reach, and stay opaque until they land;
  - like the snow, they are already in the air the first frame;
  - they use the same pool and cap, and density and motion turn them down or
    off.
  - First version: 16 drops a second, fading from the start. In the shot the
    drops hung by the nozzles and could hardly be seen, so it is now 40 a
    second, opaque for the first two thirds of the flight.
- **The tooltip** (`Describe.building`) adds "Waters 4 plots each morning"
  and "Zombies walk over it".
- **A018's Deliverables** now state the settled geometry: the three ids, each
  16x16 at (8,14), idle all day and the spray loop through the first hour,
  watering the four, the 3x3 and the 5x5.

**Tests:**

  - refused on a carrot;
  - put down on turned earth, it leaves no plot and offers no verb;

## 0179 - Fish by pond, season and hour - done 2026-10-09

What changed: the one fish became twelve species across 0156's three ponds.
Each species has its waters, seasons and hours, and a weight in the draw. A
cast now asks where and when as well as whether. The triple "rare" fish is
gone.

**The table** (`GameData.FISH_SPECIES`, in `digest()`, every field a lever):
- **`ponds`** uses 0156's names, `north_west_pond`, `forest_pond` and
  `south_east_lake`, found from a cell by `Farm.pond_of`.
- **`seasons`**.
- **`hours`**: `[from, to]` on 0126's clock (`Phases.clock_minute`),
  inclusive.
- **`weight`**.
- **The species:**
  - **Commons:** carp is all year and all day in the two western waters;
    perch and summer's tilapia keep the south-east lake; catfish bites after
    18:00 everywhere; sunfish is a summer day in the forest pond; bream is
    spring and summer, north and south.
  - **The middling three:** trout on spring and autumn mornings in the
    north-west; pike in autumn and winter in the west; eel on spring and
    summer nights in the south.
  - **The rare three**, one water, one season and a few hours each: dorado
    at midday in a south-east summer, salmon by day in a north-west autumn,
    sturgeon at night in a south-east winter.
- **Prices:** commons $7-10, the middling three $13-15, the rare three
  $22-25.
- **Deviation:** a species' value is its `SELL_PRICE` and is not repeated in
  the table, so one number cannot disagree with itself.
- **Prices kept under oil.** The first draft priced sturgeon at $40, and
  0032's "oil is the dearest thing in the ledger" check refused it. The rare
  three now sit just under oil's $26, at about three commons each. A cast
  averages about what the old $8 fish did.

**The cast** (`Fishing.begin`):
- The bite-delay draw stays, and it comes first.
- Then `Fishing.draw` takes one species from the run RNG, weighted, among
  `Fishing.catchable(pond, season, minute)` at the moment the line goes in.
- Water that names no pond would land a carp without a draw. There is none
  today: each pond's anchor is checked.
- `reel` gives one of that species, and `last_catch` is
  `{species, yield}`.
- `FISHING` keeps its bite and window levers. `rare_in`, `common_yield` and
  `rare_yield` are gone.

**Any fish, as a rule:**
- **`GameData.FISH` is the fish group now**, not a resource. It is listed in
  `ANY_OF`, the groups a cost may name.
- **The recipes keep their text.** `press_fish_oil` takes `{FISH: 3}` and
  `cook_fish` `{FISH: 1, CARROT: 1}`, both meaning any species.
- **`Resources` understands the group:**
  - `amount` is the sum of all species held;
  - `can_afford` and `missing` count them together;
  - `pay` takes members in `GameData.pay_order`, cheapest first and then by
    name, so a recipe never spends the sturgeon while there is carp.
- **Prices and checks:**
  - `_worth` prices a group at its cheapest member, so `check_chain` values a
    recipe there;
  - `check_recipes` accepts `ANY_OF` inputs.
- **The name and icon of "any fish":**
  - `ITEM_FISH` stays as the name of "fish" in a recipe line;
  - `icon_fish` stays as its icon, and `UiKit.orphan_icons` accepts an
    `ANY_OF` group's icon.

**`check_fishing`, rewritten.** Every species must:
- name real ponds, seasons and in-clock hours, with a weight of at least one;
- be a priced resource in the fish group.

And every pond must have a catch in every season at every minute of the day.
This is checked per pond and season by laying the hours end to end. A table
without carp, for example, leaves the north-west pond quiet and is refused.

**The old fish goes.** `State.VERSION` is 8. `Save._fish_by_species_v7`:
- moves `held` and `gained` fish into carp, the commonest; carp is a literal,
  so re-weighting the pond later cannot move an old save;
- reels in an open line empty;
- renames `last_catch`.

`make_goldens` wrote `run-v8.sav` and its older and newer shapes.

**The readers that followed:**
- `headless_check`, the fishing group (0030), rewritten:
  - its teeth now include the quiet pond;
  - 400 casts from one shore see every species that can bite there, the
    commonest more often than the rarest;
  - the replay log records species.
- `headless_check`, elsewhere:
  - the reference sheet's fish is carp;
  - the yield test gains carp.
- **`input_check`'s fishing case:** the catch is one fish of the drawn
  species, named in the last catch.
- **Three `headless_v1` asserts pinned to version 7** (0166, 0170, 0172) now
  read "7 or later" or the current version.

**On screen:**
- The inventory's fish tab lists the twelve, ten to a page.
- Their icons are 24 A022 stand-ins (`icon_`/`hud_` per species), today's
  fish icon tinted toward each species' colours, until 0205.
- A022's Deliverables now state the final list and the three cuts.

**Tests:**
- `_task_0179_species` (headless_v1) checks:
  - the tables pass and the plain fish is gone;
  - each pond's water knows its name;
  - 40 casts on one seed give the same species twice, and another seed gives
    others;
  - no summer-only species can bite in spring at any half hour in any pond;
  - 200 spring casts at noon on the south-east lake never land one, and 200
    summer casts do;
  - the north-west pond and the south-east lake give different sets: carp
    and trout in one and not the other;
  - reeling gives the hooked species and names it;
  - cook_fish spends a carp before a sturgeon;
  - the press takes the last carp, then a perch, then one sturgeon;
  - a cost of fish counts every species together;
  - a version 7 golden carrying 7 fish (9 gained) loads as 7 carp (9 gained)
    with no plain fish left;
  - the version 8 golden reads back.

**Notes:**
- The minigame, the rods' effects, bait and the fish book are later tasks
  (0180-0182); legendaries are 0182's.
- The inventory's tab column clips the bottom of its last tab (TOOLS), as it
  has since 0173 added that tab.

### Hashes

Both moved on purpose, accepted with `verify.py --accept`.
- **SIM 3052463561 -> 3492418464**: twelve new keys in `held` and `gained`,
  no `fish` key, and `version` 8. The fixed scenario never fishes, so the
  draw itself is not what moved it.
- **DATA 1873325290 -> 4172682401**: `FISH_SPECIES`, `ANY_OF`, the trimmed
  `FISHING`, the twelve prices, and the fish group's members.

## 0180 - The fishing minigame - done 2026-10-09

What changed: a bite now opens a bar. A marker sweeps it back and forth, and
a press while the marker is over the green counts. One to three hits, by
species, land the fish. Too many misses, or the bar running out, lose it
and nothing else. It plays the same on the keyboard, the mouse and a pad.

**The rule** (`Fishing`, all in core, nothing drawn after the cast):
- **The cast makes every draw:**
  - the bite delay;
  - the species (0179);
  - now where the green sits: `zone_at`, the last draw.
- **The green's width** is fixed at the cast as well: the species' `zone`,
  times the rod tier's `zone_percent` (100/125/150, the field 0173
  reserved), plus `assist_zone` under the assist.
- **The marker's pace** is the species' `speed` in steps a second, times
  `assist_speed_percent` under the assist.
- **The marker** is `marker_at(since, speed, bar_units)`: a triangle sweep, a
  pure function of the ticks since the bite.
- **The bite opens the bar:** `since` 0, `bar_ticks` to run.
- **A press** is the `interact` edge. `Fishing.tick` spends it while the bar
  runs, before `Player` sees it, so a strike starts no other job. It is
  judged against the marker on the tick it is spent, before the marker moves
  on, which is where the view drew it.
  - Over the green, it is a hit. Off it, it is a miss.
- **One hit a sweep** (`pass_of`). A second press on the sweep that already
  scored is spent and counts for nothing. Without this, pressing every tick
  through one crossing of the green landed a three-hit fish at once.
- **The end:** the species' `hits` land it through `reel`. More than
  `misses_allowed` misses, or `bar_ticks` running out, call `give_up`.
- **Levers:**
  - `FISHING`: `bar_units` 100, `bar_ticks` 10 s, `misses_allowed` 2,
    `assist_zone` 12, `assist_speed_percent` 60;
  - per species in `FISH_SPECIES`: `speed`, `zone`, `hits`:
    - commons: 60-66 steps a second, a green of 24-26, one hit;
    - trout, pike and eel: 84-90, 20-22, two hits;
    - the rare three: 90-96, 18, three hits.
- **`check_fishing` bounds all of them.** It refuses each of these:
  - hits outside 1-3, or a missing speed or green;
  - a green that the widest rod plus the assist would push past the bar;
  - a rod outside 50-200%;
  - a bar that would not cross the green as many times as a species needs
    hits, at the assist's slower pace too.
- `window_ticks` is gone, and `Interact`'s `reel` arm is `Fishing.strike`.

**The assist** is the run's top-level `fishing_assist` key:
- `Fishing.initial()` declares it, so `State.reconcile` fills it in for an
  old save.
- `Main` writes the `gameplay/fishing_assist` setting into
  `intent.fishing_assist` every frame, as a level. `Fishing.tick` copies it
  in. Core never reads `Settings`.
- It shapes the next cast, not the one in the water.
- The Options row is 0292's.

**Keyboard, mouse and pad - a deviation.** The prompt asked for a new action
with its own pad binding. There is no pad button free: every standard
button and both triggers already carry an action, and 0121's check refuses
two actions on one pad input. So the three devices write the existing
`interact` edge:
- SPACE or Enter, and the pad's A, through `interact` as ever;
- a click (the `place` action, mouse left) that no panel took, which
  `Main._unhandled_input` turns into the same edge while the bar is up.

No action was added, `project.godot` is untouched, and the strike is the
key that cast the line.

**The view** (`FishingBar`, a new HUD control over the night HUD):
- It is drawn at (240,184) on the 480x270 screen, under the farmer, while the
  bar runs.
- It has a timber frame with brass caps, the dark track, the green (light
  top row, dark bottom row, ink ends), the needle and the species' hits as
  pips.
- The last press flashes: a gold star for a hit, droplets for a miss.
- A023's five pieces (`fishbar_frame`, `_zone`, `_marker`, `_hit`, `_miss`)
  are registered as drawn by code until 0206.
- The farmer keeps today's `fish`/`reel` strips until A024 is integrated by
  0207.
- The HUD line reads "A BITE - PRESS ON THE GREEN" ("FISGOU - APERTE NO
  VERDE").
- `Sfx`: the bite sound stays, and `reel` keeps its verb sound.

**A024** (the pack exists, blocked by the owner's deferral of the farmer's
sprites). Its "how the game plays it" line now records what 0180
confirmed:
- a 1 s cast;
- a wait of 4.7-23 s;
- `fish_strike` once as the bar opens;
- `fish_reel` looping through a bar of up to 10 s;
- `fish_catch` held about a second on a landing, or straight back to idle.

**A023** states the bar's settled geometry:
- the frame is 100x16, with `track_xywh` (5,5,90,6) carrying the 100
  steps;
- the zone is a stretched 3-patch;
- the marker's centre column sits on its step;
- the hit and miss flashes play at the marker's x;
- the pips are drawn by code.

**What still reeled in one press, rewritten:**
- `_task_0030_fishing` lands its fish through the bar (`_land_by_bar`), and
  the window wording became the bar's.
- `_case_0030_fishing`, the art showcase's catch and its `reel` work
  fixture put the whole bar under the green and ask for one hit. Where the
  green sits is the headless suite's question; whether the press reaches the
  bar is theirs.
  - The fixture was found by the first verify. "player work" (13) and
    "player reactions" (4) failed, because a press on an unrigged bar missed
    and no catch follow-through played.
- 0166's "reaction window remains 1.5 s" now asserts the bar's 10 s.
- The determinism scenario only casts. Its line now draws the green too and
  runs its bar out unstruck.
- The autoplayer never fished.

**Tests:**
- `_task_0180_minigame` (headless_v1):
  - the levers pass, and their teeth refuse four hits, a green wider than
    the bar and a bar too short;
  - a press a tick before the green is a miss, spent by the bar and not by
    `Player`, and the next tick's lands a carp;
  - pressing every tick over the green scores once a sweep, and the
    sturgeon's third hit lands it;
  - the assist's intent sets the run's flag, widens the green and slows the
    marker, and the iron rod widens it again;
  - a bar nobody strikes at runs out with nothing taken, and one miss over
    the allowance loses the fish;
  - a replay with the same presses lands the same fish on the same tick;
  - the RNG does not move between the bite and the catch.
- `_case_0180_minigame` (input_v1): a fish landed with SPACE, with a click on
  the farm and with a synthetic pad A. Each time the bar is up while it runs
  and gone with the fish.
- `headless_check` asks for one shot per scenario: 63 now.

### Hashes

Both moved on purpose, accepted with `verify.py --accept`.
- **SIM 3492418464 -> 1648872965**: the cast's new draw (where the green
  sits), the line's new fields, and the run's `fishing_assist` key and
  intent field. The scenario's line now runs its bar out unstruck.
- **DATA 4172682401 -> 1985581423**: the bar's levers in `FISHING` (the
  window gone) and `speed`, `zone` and `hits` on every species.

Verify: 60 passed, 0 failed in 649s (the known OVER BUDGET), on the second full run.
headless_check 17085, headless_v1 1704 (+12), input_check 1167, input_v1
507 (+13), player work 25761 checks, player reactions 676, placeholders

## 0181 - Rods and bait - done 2026-10-09

What changed: the rod's tier now changes what bites. Fibre brings the bite
sooner and the rarer fish more often; iron does both again, has the slot a
bait goes in, and is the one rod a legendary will take (0182's gate). The hoe
turns up worms, the workshop cuts a fish into bait, and with the iron rod the
bait that is on goes on the hook at the cast.

**The rod** (`TOOLS` rod, the 0173 fields, now read):
- `bite_percent` scales the bite range at the cast: bamboo 100, fibre 80,
  iron 65 of `bite_min_ticks`-`bite_max_ticks`.
- `rare_percent` multiplies the draw weight of every species that is not
  common: bamboo 100, fibre 125, iron 150.
- `bait_slot` (iron only) is `Fishing.has_bait_slot`, and `legendary` (iron
  only) is `Fishing.takes_legendary`, the gate 0182 checks.

**Rarity:** each `FISH_SPECIES` entry has a `tier` from `FISH_TIERS`:
- common: carp, perch, tilapia, catfish, sunfish, bream;
- uncommon: trout, pike, eel;
- rare: dorado, salmon, sturgeon.

`Fishing.weight_of` is the species' weight, times the cast's `rare_percent`
when it is not common. `draw` takes that percent, and at 100 every weight is
what it was, so a bamboo cast draws exactly as before.

**The bait:**
- `WORM` and `BAIT` are resources, $1 and $2. They have their own inventory
  group, `bait` (BAIT / ISCAS), right after the fish. They are not in the fish
  group: that group is `ANY_OF`, and a recipe taking any fish pays the
  cheapest first, so a $2 bait would have been cooked as a fish.
- `BAIT_EFFECTS`: a worm is a 60% wait; fish bait is 200% on the rarer fish.
- Spent at the cast, in `Fishing.begin`, by a rod with the slot when one is
  held. It records `line["bait"]`. The wait range is the rod's percent times
  the bait's, and so is `rare_percent`.
- **No bait is no effect, never a refusal.** With none held, or on a bamboo
  or fibre rod, the line goes in plain and nothing is spent.
- **Which bait is on** is the run's top-level `fishing_bait` (`&""`, `worm`
  or `bait`), like `selected_seed`. It is not in `State.TABLES`, because it
  is not a nested dictionary. `State.reconcile` fills it in for an old save
  from `Fishing.initial()`.
  - `choose_bait` refuses anything that is not a bait.
  - `step_bait` goes round none, worm and fish bait, both ways.

**Worms:** `Farming._till` draws `Rng.chance(1, WORM_IN)` for each cell it
turns (`WORM_IN` 8, a lever in `digest()`). The draw is in `_till`, not in
`_till_one`, which clearing a crop shares: REMOVE draws nothing.

**The recipe** (a decision the prompt left open): `make_bait` at the
**workshop**, beside the other supplies it makes: the kits, the gunpowder and
the incendiary rounds.
- It takes `{FISH: 1}`, any fish cheapest first, so the commons go first.
- It makes 4 bait in 5/240 of a day, on the CRAFT tab.
- `check_chain` passes: $8 of bait from a $7 fish.
- 0166's daily budget table gained its row: 48 batches and 192 bait a day,
  nominal.
- **The kitchen was the first choice, and the first verify refused it.**
  0034's "makes food" assert holds every kitchen recipe to making food, which
  is the kitchen's job in the MVP. Bait is gear, not food, so it moved rather
  than that rule bending.
- The workshop's first recipe is still the barricade kit (by name, `make_bait`
  sorts after `fence_kit`).

**`check_bait`** (in `validate()`) refuses each of these:
- a bait that is not a priced resource in the bait group;
- a choice list and an effect table that disagree;
- a rod tier or bait whose wait is outside 25-100%, or whose rarer-fish
  percent is outside 100-400%;
- a best rod and bait that would bite in under a second (iron and worm: 54
  ticks);
- a worm in every cell;
- a species with no tier.

**The view:**
- `DayHud`'s `BaitButton` sits at (186,220), under the fishing line. It shows
  "BAIT  worm x2  (Q/E)" ("ISCA  minhoca x2  (Q/E)"), or "BAIT  none" with
  the keys for the device in hand.
- It is up by day, outdoors with no panel open, with the iron rod, while the
  farmer faces water or has a line waiting. It hides over the bar, where a
  press strikes.
- A click steps it. So do Q/E (the shoulder buttons on a pad), which
  `DayHud._unhandled_input` takes while the button is up. By day those
  actions were free: the night hotbar is hidden, and the open inventory takes
  them first in `_input`.
- `focus_mode` is NONE, so SPACE casts rather than pressing it.
- No new action and no `project.godot` change.
- The icons are A023's `icon_worm`/`hud_worm`/`icon_bait`/`hud_bait`, through

## 0182 - Legendary fish and the fish book - done 2026-10-09

What changed: four legendary fish, one a season, bite only on the iron rod,
in their own water and hours, under their own condition, once a run, on the
hardest bar there is. Every fish landed now writes a page in the run's fish
book, the profile keeps the counts across runs, and the ledger's last tab is
the book: a page per species, a silhouette and a hint for the ones never
caught, and the collection count over it.

**The four** (`FISH_SPECIES`, ids as A022 names them, `tier` `legendary`):

| Season | Legendary | Water | Hours | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| spring | Old Catfish (Velho Bagre) | forest pond | 20:00-02:00 | a Full Moon day |
| summer | Golden Queen (Rainha Dourada) | south-east lake | 11:00-14:00 | a worm on the hook |
| autumn | Ghost Pike (Lúcio Fantasma) | north-west pond | 22:00-02:00 | fish bait on the hook |
| winter | Ice Sturgeon (Esturjão de Gelo) | south-east lake | 06:00-09:00 | a Full Moon day |

- `condition` is one of `FISH_CONDITIONS`: `full_moon` (the date is one of
  `FULL_MOON_DAYS`), or a bait id, meaning that bait went on the hook at this
  cast.
  - It is called `condition` and not `needs`, because 0180's line already
    uses `needs` for the hits a fish takes.
- Each has weight 2, against 12-30 for the commons. With the iron rod's
  `rare_percent` that is 3, and 6 with fish bait.
- **The hardest bar:** 3 hits, speed 108 and a green of 14. The fastest
  other species is 96, the narrowest green 18.
- Each sells for $25, like the sturgeon. Oil stays the dearest thing in the
  ledger (0032's rule); what a legendary is worth is its page.
- **`check_fishing` (`_check_legendaries`)** refuses each of these:
  - a legendary in more or fewer than one season, or two in one season, or
    a season without one;
  - a condition outside `FISH_CONDITIONS`, or a `condition` on anything that
    is not a legendary;
  - a bar easier than any other species';
  - a weight as high as the lightest common's.
  - The pond-coverage rule now skips legendaries: they cover no hour,
    because they only bite when their condition holds.

**The rule** (`Fishing`):
- `catchable` no longer returns legendaries.
- `legendaries_at(state, pond, season, minute, bait)` adds them at the cast,
  each one only if all of these hold:
  - the rod takes a legendary (`takes_legendary`, the iron rod's `legendary`
    from 0181);
  - the pond, season and hours are its own;
  - `condition_met` holds;
  - **once a run** (decided): the run's book does not have it yet.
- `begin` draws from both lists. On a bamboo or fibre rod the list is the
  same as before, so those draws do not move.

**The book:**
- The state's `fish_book` maps species to `{caught, first_day}`, the first
  day being the calendar date. Its keys come from play, so it is in
  `State.RUN_DATA`. `reel` writes it, for every species, commons included.
- `Stats.of_run` and `lifetime` gain `fish_book`. `Stats.fold` banks it
  like `killed_by_kind`, so folding twice adds nothing.
- `Stats.fish_known(profile, state)` is the profile's counts plus whatever
  the run has landed since its last fold. The page counts a fish caught a
  minute ago, before the night banks it.
- **Found in passing, fixed:** `reel` has written `last_catch` since task
  0030, but `Fishing.initial()` never declared it, so `State.reconcile`
  dropped it on every load. It is declared now (in `RUN_DATA`). The
  save-round-trip assert below would not pass without it.

**The view** (`FishBook`, new `src/ui/fish_book.gd`, in the inventory):
- The ledger's last tab, FISH BOOK (LIVRO DE PEIXES), after TOOLS. It has 16
  pages, one per species, in the fish group's order: commons, the middling
  three, the rare three, then the legendaries.
- They turn with the rest of the ledger: Q/E, the shoulder buttons, and the
  arrow buttons. From the ledger's first page, Q wraps round to the book's
  last.
- A page shows, from the top:
  - the collection count, "4 OF 16 COLLECTED" ("4 DE 16 NA COLEÇÃO");
  - the 32x32 portrait;
  - the name, or "? ? ?" for an unknown species;
  - the rarity, LEGENDARY in the good colour;
  - the hint;
  - "caught N in every run", or "never caught yet";
  - "this run: the first on SPRING 7", or "none yet this run";
  - the price, for a known species.
- An unknown species is its portrait drawn black.
- The 16 hints are hand-written rows (`BOOK_HINT_*`), each with a 300 px
  budget that `tools/i18n_check.py` measures in both languages. Three
  Portuguese hints were shortened to fit.
- `Main` hands the profile to the inventory (`_show_profile`) everywhere it
  handed it to the statistics screen.
- **Art, through 0120's road:**
  - A022's `portrait_<id>` for all 16: each species' tinted `icon_fish`
    stand-in, at twice the size (`stand_in_scale` 2, `PORTRAIT` 32x32 at
    (16,16)).
  - `icon_`/`hud_` for the four legendaries:
    - mossy for the Old Catfish;
    - gold for the Golden Queen;
    - pale for the Ghost Pike;
    - ice blue for the Ice Sturgeon.
  - A023's `hud_book_fish` on the tab: the fish icon, untinted. A tab's icon
    wears the theme's colours, and headless_check refuses a screen that
    overrides them. The first try did, and the check caught it.
  - `UiKit.picture(name)` loads any of them.
  - A022's and A023's docs say how 0182 uses them.

### Hashes

- **SIM 3238533707 -> 42882243, on purpose.** The state gained
  `fish_book` and the declared `last_catch`, and four new resources in
  `held` and `gained`. The determinism scenario casts on the bamboo rod,
  whose draw is unchanged.
- **DATA 3325784326 -> 1812557335, on purpose.** The new data:
  - the four legendaries in `FISH_SPECIES`, `RESOURCES`, `SELL_PRICE` and
    the fish group;
  - `legendary` in `FISH_TIERS`;
  - `FISH_CONDITIONS`, in `digest()`.

Verify: 60 passed, 0 failed in 754s (the known OVER BUDGET): headless_check 17173 asserts, headless_v1 1785, input_check 1179 cases, input_v1 609, sim 42882243, data 1812557335.

**Tests:**

  - **Data:** the levers pass. Their teeth refuse a condition no cast meets,

  - **The rod gate**, 600 casts a rod into the forest pond on Spring 7 at

  - **Its conditions:** 0 on the day before the Full Moon, at noon, in the

  - **The other three:** the Golden Queen bites on a worm and not on fish

  - **Landed:** the Old Catfish is drawn naturally on an iron cast, and its

  - **Once a run:** 600 more casts never draw it, and `legendaries_at` is

## 0183 - The coop and the barn - done 2026-10-09

What changed: animals have homes. A coop and a barn go up by day, the first
of each takes in the map's loose chickens or cow, and their produce is
collected at the door. Until one is built, the map's animals stand and work
exactly as before.

**The buildings** (`BUILDINGS`, all levers; footprints and capacities
decided here):

| | Size | Holds | HP | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| coop | 3x2 | 4 chickens | 60 | 30 wood, 10 stone, $80 |
| barn | 5x4 | 4 animals | 100 | 60 wood, 25 stone, $200 |

- Both fit 0156's 7x4 sites, and anywhere else buildable.
- `BLD_COOP`/`BLD_BARN` name them ("galinheiro", "celeiro").
- `Describe.building` adds "Houses 4 animals" ("Abriga 4 animais").

**The rule** (`Livestock`):
- `LIVESTOCK` gains `home` (cow: barn, chicken: coop) and `source`, which
  is `map` or `stall` (0190's), from `LIVESTOCK_SOURCES`.
- **`housed`** is a new state key, listed in `State.RUN_DATA`. It maps a
  home's anchor index to `{home, animals: [{id, ready, left}]}`. Housed
  animals tick on the loose ones' clock (`_produce`, shared), home by home in
  cell order.
- **`move_in`** runs from `Building.place` for a home:
  - the map's loose animals of its kind, in cell order, up to its capacity:
    removed from `occupants` and `livestock`, with what they had waiting and
    their timers;
  - then any animals in `unhoused`;
  - **one `Farm.touch`** for all of them.
  - Every home runs it, so a second coop would take in any loose hens the
    first had no room for.
- **`house(state, cell, kind)`** is the one way in. It refuses an animal of
  another home, or a full home. 0190's stall will deliver through it.
- **The door** is the middle cell of the front row: (1,1) on the coop and
  (2,3) on the barn (`door_of`).
  - Only the door offers `collect`, and only while someone inside has
    something waiting. The farmer stands below it, facing north. Collecting
    takes everyone's produce.
  - `Interact._offered` asks `Livestock` for homes as for loose animals, and
    a damaged home still offers `repair` first.
- **No animal is ever lost:**
  - If a home's anchor is cleared (`Farm.forget_cell` -> `Livestock.forget_cell`),
    its animals go to **`unhoused`**, a new top-level list. They wait there,
    producing nothing, until the next home of their kind takes them in.
  - Selling a home with animals in it is refused (`WHY_HOME_IN_USE`, "Animals
    live here" / "Tem animais morando aqui").
  - 0186 turns a destroyed home into a wrecked one that keeps its animals, so
    `unhoused` becomes rare.
- **`check_livestock`** is reworked. Each kind names a home with room, and
  its source is `map` or `stall`. Only a `map` kind must stand on the map:
  "every animal stands on the map" is no longer a rule. Every home must house
  some kind.
- **Saves:** a save with loose animals keeps working. Reconcile fills
  `housed` and `unhoused`, and its cow and chickens stand and produce as
  before. No version bump.

**The view:**
- The coop and barn are drawn through 0120's road. `_stand_in_prop` now
  takes `sprites/buildings/` entries too.
  - The coop is the kitchen at 0.6 (1.2 on screen), warm-tinted.
  - The barn is the workshop at 0.9 (1.8), barn-red.
  - Both sit at A030's canvases: 64x64 at (32,60) and 96x100 at (48,96).
- Housed animals are drawn by `WorldView._draw_housed`, view only:
  - along the row below the building, either side of the door, one per
    cell, then a second row a step behind;
  - with the loose animals' ambient motion.
  - The farm redraws on a signature of who lives where, not on the timers.
- At dusk `Transition` fades them with the loose ones. They carry a
  `day_only` meta, and its cache now also watches the number of drawings in
  the occupants layer, because a hen moving in changes no occupant count.
- The day build list has nine rows now, all on screen (`build_day` shot).
  The barn sorts first, so it is the list's default selection.
- **A030's Deliverables** now state the settled footprints, capacities, the
  door cell and where the farmer collects, and that the points stand.

**What did not need changing:** `_task_0034_cooking`, `_case_0034_livestock`,
`_task_0038_idle` and the determinism scenario all use the map's loose
animals, which behave as they always did while no home exists. No other
suite needed a rewrite.

### Hashes

- **SIM 42882243 -> 735944060, on purpose.** The state gained `housed`
  and `unhoused`. The determinism scenario's animals are the map's loose
  ones and do as they did; it builds no home.
- **DATA 1812557335 -> 91621100, on purpose:**
  - the coop and the barn in `BUILDINGS`;
  - `home` and `source` on each `LIVESTOCK` kind;
  - `LIVESTOCK_SOURCES`, in `digest()`.
- **The first verify failed perf alone:** path_refresh at 13132 us
  against a baseline of 8782, view_particles and night_towers up as much.
  - The owner's WelcomeBackHero build (one_room_dg) was holding a full
    core.
  - An A/B under that same load, the 0182 commit in a scratch worktree
    against this tree, gave path_refresh of 13556 and 11890 us for 0182
    and 12285 and 13373 for 0183: the same.
  - The next verify passed perf at 10317 us. The baseline was not touched.

Verify: 60 passed, 0 failed in 733s (the known OVER BUDGET), on the third run: headless_check 17180 asserts, headless_v1 1807, input_check 1181 cases, input_v1 615, sim 735944060, data 91621100. The first failed perf under the load above; the second failed `_case_0183_barn`'s gliding click, fixed as told under Tests.

**Tests:**
- `_task_0183_barns` (headless_v1):
  - **Data:** the homes and sources pass. Their teeth refuse a cow living in
    a kitchen, a chicken from nowhere, and a barn nobody lives in. A stall
    animal that is not on the map passes.
  - **Move-in:** a coop on its site takes both map chickens off the map,
    with one hen's waiting produce. The farm is touched exactly once beyond

  - **The door** is (1,1) from any of the coop's cells. Only it offers

  - **A knocked-down coop** leaves its 4 hens in `unhoused`, and the next

  - **Saves:** with no barn the cow works as before. The v8 golden loads

- `_case_0183_barn` (input_v1):
  - B opens build mode by day. The coop's row is on screen; a click selects

  - The map's two chickens move in, and its description says it houses 4.

  - **It aimed at the coop's site first, and the click missed twice.**

Looked at (`python tools/shot.py 0183 coop_barn --fhd`, 1920x1080):

## 0184 - Feeding, eggs and milk - done 2026-10-09

What changed: the animals now give what they are kept for, and the housed
ones eat.
- Hens lay eggs and cows give milk.
- Every wheat harvest leaves straw, and the workshop turns straw into hay.
- Each morning every housed animal eats a bale. One that goes without gives
  nothing that day, and is still there, no worse, the next.

**The goods** (all levers; four new resources):

| Resource | Price | Inventory tab | Comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| straw | $1 | materials | 3 per wheat harvest (wheat's `byproduct`) |
| hay | $2 | materials | `make_hay` at the workshop: 1 straw into 1 hay in 3/240 of a day |
| egg | $4 | animal goods | chickens, at their old rate and `holds` |
| milk | $9 | animal goods | cows, at their old rate and `holds` |

- `check_crops` refuses a byproduct that is no resource.
- **Where the hay is made.** The prompt left the station open:
  - the press was out, because 0032 holds every press recipe to making oil;
  - the kitchen was out, because 0034 holds every kitchen recipe to making
    food (0181 met the same rule);
  - the workshop stands on every farm from the first morning, and its craft
    list scrolls.
  - 0166's daily budget table gained `make_hay`: 80 batches and 80 hay a
    day, nominal.

**Feeding** (`Livestock`):
- `ANIMAL_FEED` is hay, and each kind eats `feed_per_day` of it: 1 for both,
  levers.
- `Phases.begin_day` calls `Livestock.feed` after the other mornings. Every
  housed animal eats, home by home in cell order and each in the order it
  moved in, while there is enough. It records `fed` on the animal's entry in
  `housed`.
- An unfed animal's clock does not run that day. What it had waiting stays
  to be collected. It never dies or sickens.
- **Decided: day 1 counts as fed.**
  - An animal is fed the day it moves in (`house` writes `fed: true`), and
    no morning has come before day 1.
  - A hen off the grass has grazed, and 0190's bought ones arrive fed.
  - The first bale is due the next morning.
- **Decided: the map's loose animals graze.** They are never fed and never
  hungry, exactly as before.
  - So `_task_0034_cooking`, `_case_0034_livestock`, `_task_0038_idle` ("the
    animals produced", `_a_busy_day`, which counts what is waiting, of
    whatever kind) and the determinism scenario's animals still produce.
- `Describe.building` adds "Each eats 1 hay a day" to the coop and the barn.

**The meat decision:**
- `MEAT` stays, and so does `cook_roast`. It is bought at the stall:
  `DAILY_STOCK` now carries 6 a day, at the usual markup, so a bought meat
  sold straight back still loses money.
- No animal gives meat any more. A save's waiting produce is a count, so it
  comes out as the new product: a cow with 2 waiting gives 2 milk. No
  version bump.
- **`check_livestock` follows the decision** and refuses each of these:
  - a farm where no animal gives meat and the stall sells none (it takes the
    stock as a parameter now);
  - a kind that says nothing of what it eats;
  - a feed that nothing makes, neither a recipe nor the stall.
- **For 0190**, which turns the stall's stock seasonal: keep meat in every

## 0186 - Barns at night - done 2026-10-10

What changed: the night can now take a coop or a barn away for a day, and
never for good.
- Breakers already hunted them, being buildings with no `path_cost`. That is
  now asserted.
- At 0 HP a coop or a barn is **wrecked, never lost**. It stands dark and out
  of use, its animals inside, until it is mended by day.
- No animal ever dies.

**The rule** (`wrecks`, `src/core/`):
- `wrecks: true` is on the coop and the barn in `BUILDINGS`, read by
  `Building.wrecks`. Nothing else declares it.
- **One count of hit points over the whole footprint** (decided).
  - `Farm.place` gives each cell its own `hp`, and a breaker gnaws one cell.
    Every one of a barn's twenty cells would have had to be bitten to 0.
  - So for a `wrecks` building, `Farm.damage` takes the bite on the shared
    count (`Building.set_shared_hp`). `Repair.apply` mends every cell at
    once.
- **At 0** (`Farm._wreck`):
  - The occupant stays, marked `wrecked`: still a wall, no rubble.
  - `Pathing.prey_cells` already skips 0 HP. The hunt field is cached on
    `grid_version`, so the wreck calls `Farm.touch`, and so does mending it
    back above 0. Without that, breakers stand at a dead barn all night.
- **It counts as a structure lost** (decided): `Run.lost_a_structure`, the
  run's tally that its summary and the stats show.
  - The morning report's "came down" line counts tonight's rubble, and a
    wreck leaves none. It stands, and the report leaves it out.
  - The event is `structure_lost` with `wrecked: true`.
  - The log reads "Barn wrecked - mend it by day" ("Celeiro arrasado -
    conserte de dia").
- **Out of use** (`Livestock`):
  - It offers no `collect` and gives nothing.
  - The morning's hay feeds nobody in it and none is spent: its animals are
    marked unfed.
  - Its pigs mark no spots, and its animals' clocks do not run.
  - Its door offers only `repair`: by day by the farmer, and at night by the
    guardian, 0134's one night verb.
- **Any hit point brings it back.**
  - Nothing is removed, so `Farm.forget_cell` never runs.
  - `Crafting`'s queues and `Livestock`'s residents stay where they were. The
    residents are asserted.

**The view:**
- **Hurt and wrecked looks** (`WorldView._worn_home`): `<id>_hurt` under
  three quarters and `<id>_wreck` at 0, A030's names.
  - They are registered on 0120's road: the kitchen's and the workshop's own
    hurt art, tinted like the whole stand-in for hurt and dark for the
    wreck, until 0212.
- **Animals inside:** `AnimalView` hides a wrecked home's animals by day too.
  At night `Transition` already fades all of them.
- **The lantern** (`Lighting`, new):
  - A standing coop or barn, whole or hurt, has a small warm lantern lit at
    night, left of its door at about the farmer's head. It goes dark once
    the building is wrecked.
  - A030's `light_xy` takes over when the art lands, and its `windows_xy`
    light up once measured.
  - Two reasons. A030 promised it ("0186 lights and wrecks the buildings"),
    and the picture asked for it: at night the tints alone barely told hurt
    from wrecked.
- **One smoke for a wreck** (`Particles`):
  - A cell under two fifths smokes, so a barn at 0 smoked from all twenty
    cells: a grid of ghosts over its roof in the first picture.
  - A `wrecks` building now smokes from one point.

**Art settled:** one sentence in A030's Deliverables now states 0186's rules:
- hit points shared over the footprint;
- the hurt and wreck thresholds;
- the lantern and windows lit on whole and hurt only;
- where the wreck smokes.

### Hashes

- **SIM 216342093 unchanged:** the determinism scenario has no barn at
  night. The prompt said to say so.
- **DATA 1869696351 -> 4133877013, on purpose:** `wrecks` on the coop and
  the barn.

Verify: 60 passed, 0 failed in 649s (the known OVER BUDGET), with `--accept`:
headless_check 17283 asserts, headless_v1 1892, input_check 1193 cases,
input_v1 631, effects 2997, sim 216342093 unchanged and data 1869696351 ->
4133877013 recorded. The run before the lantern failed the data hash alone.

**Tests:**
- `_task_0186_barns_night` (headless_v1):
  - **Data:** only the coop and the barn wreck, and both are prey with no
    `path_cost`.
  - **The night:** a barn with the map's cow and a sheep, a parked night, and
    three breakers set down beside it. They wreck it:
    - every cell at 0, marked, standing, no rubble;
    - no longer prey, with the hunt field told (`grid_version` moved);
    - one structure lost, and every animal still inside;
    - its door offers only `repair`, and its lantern is dark.
  - **They move on:** they go on to other prey (prey HP falls), and the wreck

  - **The next morning:**
    - no hay spent and nobody fed;
    - the sheep's clock gives nothing all day;
    - every animal there, `repair` only.
  - **The repair:**
    - One day repair (`Interact.complete`) brings it back: prey again, the

    - The next morning the sheep eats and gives its wool.
- `headless_check` asks for one shot per scenario: 68 now (`barn_night`).

Looked at (`python tools/shot.py 0186 barn_night --fhd`, 1920x1080):

  - The site's barn wrecked: dark, one smoke at its roof, no lantern.

  - the log telling the night: wrecked, dawn, survived.

Four takes, each changed by the picture before it:
- **Ghosts and two wrecks.** A grid of twenty "ghosts" over the barn turned
  out to be the per-cell smoke. And both barns were wrecked: the breakers
  set at the hurt one's walls finished it during the settle.
- **No breakers in the picture.** `shot.py`'s `SimDriver` runs in real time
  under the settle, up to ten ticks a frame on a loaded machine, so any
  breaker near the hurt barn makes the picture a race. The test proves that
  they come.
- **The camera follows the farmer.** Standing him east put the barns under
  the seed bag's page, so he stands below the wreck.
- **The lantern**, because the tints alone barely told hurt from wreck at
  night.

## 0187 - Days in a barrel: the keg and the preserves jar - done 2026-10-10

What changed: the first artisan machines. A keg and a preserves jar, built
by day, turn the farm's fruit and vegetables into wine, juice, jelly and
pickles over days. These goods are worth more than anything a single day
makes.

**Days, not ticks** (`Crafting`):
- A `RECIPES` entry may say `days` instead of `ticks`. `check_recipes`
  accepts exactly one of the two, and refuses a recipe that takes no time.
- **The count:**
  - A batch pays for its inputs when it starts, as every job does.
  - `Crafting.morning`, called from `Phases.begin_day` after the tools'
    morning, takes a day off it. The tick never does.
  - So the wine is ready on its seventh morning, whatever the farmer did
    with the days between.
- **The queue:**
  - A batch on its last morning is delivered and recorded.
  - The next batch in the queue steps up and pays, and its first day is
    the next morning.
  - A batch still waiting on its inputs is started by the day's ticks, as
    before. A morning does not count it.
- **Neither "steady hands" nor a brownout touches days** (decided): a
  barrel ages at its own pace.
- **What the player reads:**
  - The panel says "make wine  5 days left" ("fazer vinho  faltam 5 dias",
    `WORK_AGING`, with a plural form).
  - A recipe's tooltip says "takes 7 days" (`DESC_DAYS`).

**The machines** (`BUILDINGS`, every number a lever):

| | Size | HP | Cost | Makes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| keg | 2x2 | 60 | 30 wood, 3 iron, $50 | wine from 3 grapes in 7 days; juice from 3 melons in 4 |
| preserves jar | 2x2 | 50 | 20 stone, 10 wood, $50 | jelly from 3 strawberries in 3 days; pickles from 3 peppers in 3 |

- **The crops** (decided): one artisan crop per growing season, so every
  season feeds a machine. Winter lives off the barrels.
  - spring: strawberry;
  - summer: melon and pepper;
  - autumn: grape.
- One recipe per good, because a recipe has fixed inputs.
- They are built by day, as every `BUILDINGS` entry is. The day build list
  has eleven rows now, all on screen (`build_day`).
- Their names are `BLD_KEG` ("barril") and `BLD_PRESERVES_JAR` ("pote de
  conserva", the plan's "conserva" with the word that makes it a thing).

**The goods:**
- WINE $60, JUICE $45, JELLY $40, PICKLES $25 (levers).
- They are in `artisan_goods` beside food and oil, named in both languages:
  vinho, suco, geleia, picles.
- **Above oil, on purpose** (decided):
  - Plan section 3.5 says a wine sells for far more than its grapes, and
    grapes are $22 against oil's $26.
  - 0032's "oil is the dearest thing in the ledger" now means the dearest
    thing a day makes. `headless_check` leaves out the goods that come out
    of a days recipe, and asserts that only those are left out.
- **A margin worth the days** (`AGED_MARGIN_PER_DAY`, a new lever, 10):
  `check_chain` asks a days recipe to add at least $10 a batch for every
  morning it holds its machine.

  | Recipe | Adds | Over | A morning |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | wine | $114 | 7 mornings | $16 |
  | juice | $60 | 4 | $15 |
  | jelly | $60 | 3 | $20 |
  | pickles | $48 | 3 | $16 |

**At 0 HP a machine is wrecked, not rubble** (decided). Both carry 0186's
`wrecks: true`.
- **Why:** a keg holds a week of grapes, and rubble would pour it out in one
  night.
- **What a wrecked machine does:**
  - It stands, with one count of hit points over its footprint and no
    rubble. It counts as a structure lost in the run's tally.
  - Its batch stays inside and ages nothing: no morning credit, no tick,
    and no new batch (`can_queue` refuses).
  - It offers only repair. `Interact` gives a wrecked station no `craft`,
    and its panel stays shut.
- **Any hit point brings it back**, and the mornings it lost come after.
- 0188 adds the `<id>_wreck` rows to A031; the stand-ins are already
  registered.

**The view:**
- **Stand-ins** (0120's road, until 0213):
  - the keg is the press, oak-dark, at 0.5 (1.0 on screen);
  - the jar is the generator, brick-red, at 0.42;
  - each machine has an idle, working, hurt and wrecked stand-in, on A031's
    provisional 48x56 canvas (`MACHINE_SMALL`).
- **States** (`WorldView`):
  - A stand-in station joins the stations' 0.12 s refresh. It swaps to its
    state's stand-in when it starts or stops working, is hurt or is
    wrecked (`_stand_in_station_art`: wear first, then work).
  - `station_running` now covers every station with a recipe, never a
    wrecked one.
  - Real-art stations are registered by the same rule, so 0213 changes no
    code.
- **The jar's small fire and stovepipe smoke** while it works (`Lighting`,
  `Particles`). They come from the footprint's middle until A031's points
  land. An idle jar smokes only as a wreck.
- **A032's icons** (until 0214):
  - wine is the oil barrel in wine-red;
  - juice is the incendiary can in orange;
  - jelly and pickles are the food bowl, red and green.

### Hashes

- **SIM 216342093 -> 788609249, on purpose:**
  - the four goods in `held` and `gained`;
  - the keg and the jar in `selected_recipe`.
- **DATA 4133877013 -> 178413484, on purpose:**
  - the four goods, their prices and their group;
  - the four recipes;
  - the two machines;
  - `AGED_MARGIN_PER_DAY` in `digest()`.

## 0188 - The dairy, the loom and the mill - done 2026-10-10

What changed: three more artisan machines.
- The dairy makes butter and cheese from milk.
- The loom makes cloth from wool, and sandbags from cloth.
- The mill makes flour from wheat and sugar from beet.

Jelly now takes the mill's sugar. Packs A031 and A032 are settled.

**The machines** (`BUILDINGS`, every number a lever):

| | Size | HP | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| dairy | 3x2 | 70 | 40 wood, 10 stone, $120 |
| loom | 3x2 | 60 | 50 wood, 4 iron, $120 |
| mill | 3x3 | 90 | 60 wood, 30 stone, $200 |

- They are built by day, and breakers hunt them.
- They wreck rather than fall, as 0187 decided for machines.
- None draws power: the wind turns the mill.
- Their names are "laticínios", "tear" and "moinho".

**The recipes** (levers):

| Recipe | At | In | Out | Time | Worth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| make_butter | dairy | 2 milk | 1 butter | 1/20 of a day | $18 -> $22 |
| make_cheese | dairy | 3 milk | 3 cheese | 2 mornings | $27 -> $60 |
| make_cloth | loom | 1 wool | 1 cloth | 1/12 of a day | $10 -> $15 |
| make_sandbag | loom | 1 cloth, 4 stone | 4 sandbags | 1/24 of a day | $27 -> $32 |
| make_flour | mill | 1 wheat | 1 flour | 1/40 of a day | $4 -> $7 |
| make_sugar | mill | 1 beet | 3 sugar | 1/24 of a day | $11 -> $15 |

- **Butter is churned by the tick and cheese ages two mornings** (decided):
  the dairy's quick money and its slow money.
- **Prices:** CHEESE 20, BUTTER 22, CLOTH 15, SANDBAG 8, FLOUR 7, SUGAR 5.
  - The goods made within a day stay under oil (0032's rule, narrowed by
    0187).
  - The cheese is aged, and `check_chain` asks its two mornings for $20; it
    adds $33.
- **The sandbag's filler is stone** (decided): what a farm has by the
  cartload.
- **Groups:** the sandbag is a material, and its night use is 0231's. The
  rest are artisan goods.
- **0166's daily budget** has five new rows, one per new recipe timed by the
  tick.

**Jelly takes sugar** (decided; plan section 3.1: "beterraba vira açúcar
para geleias", beet becomes sugar for jellies):
- `make_jelly` is now 3 strawberries and 1 sugar into 3 jelly: $65 into
  $120, still more than the $30 its three mornings ask.
- **The stall stocks 10 sugar a day**, at $13. A first spring has no
  autumn's beets behind it, and without the stall's sugar it could make no
  jelly.

**Art settled:**
- **A031**, final geometry, as the game's `BUILDINGS` sizes:
  - **footprints and canvases:** the keg and the jar 2x2 at 48x56 (24,52),
    the dairy and the loom 3x2 at 64x64 (32,60), the mill 3x3 at 64x96
    (32,92);
  - **four states each** (idle, active, hurt, wreck): 20 frames, from
    four-cell state sheets;
  - **the wreck:** every row names its `_wreck` and says what is broken.
    The wreck bullet says it stands on its idle base, inside the footprint,
    and reads as broken past hurt;
  - **points:** the jar's are on idle, active and hurt, none on the wreck;
  - acceptance, method and delivery are updated to match.
- **A032:** the eleven rows stand as written, and the ids are final: wine,
  juice, jelly and pickles (0187); cheese, butter, cloth, sandbag, flour and
  sugar (0188); bread (0192).

**Stand-ins** (0120's road, until 0213 and 0214):
- **Machines**, each idle, working, hurt and wrecked, on A031's settled
  canvases (`MACHINE_WIDE`, `MACHINE_TALL`):
  - the dairy is the kitchen in cream;
  - the loom is the workshop in cloth blue;
  - the mill is the press at 0.85, weathered grey.
- **Icons:**
  - cheese is the meat's slab in yellow;
  - butter is the food's bowl in pale yellow;
  - cloth is the logs in blue;
  - the sandbag is the stone in tan;
  - flour is the gunpowder's heap in white;
  - sugar is the coins in white.

## 0189 - The shipping bin - done 2026-10-10

What changed: a shipping bin stands by the porch. The farmer drops stacks in
at any hour of the day and is paid the next morning, so selling no longer
waits on the stall's hours (plan section 3.6).

**A fixture, not a building** (decided):
- **Why:** Stardew's bin is one, and the farm has it from the first morning.
  A player who had to build the bin would first have to know it exists.
- **What that gives:** it is in `Farm.FIXTURES`, so it is never sold, never
  wrecked, and nothing hunts it.
- **Where:** one cell at (43,26), on the 2x1 site 0156 kept by the porch,
  between the house's corner and the stall. The site's other cell is left to
  stand on.
  - `FARM_MAP` lays it with a new legend character, `B`.
  - `check_sites` now lets a site hold what it was kept for.
- **The cost: `State.VERSION` 8 -> 9.**
  - `Save._shipping_bin_v8` lays the bin on its site where an older farm's
    cell is still the empty map ground a new farm has there: no occupant,
    no plot, the same terrain.
  - A farm that put something on the site keeps it and has no bin.
  - `make_goldens` wrote `run-v9.sav` and its older and newer shapes. The
    v8 goldens stay, as the road an old save travels.

**The rule** (`Shipping`, new):
- **What waits:** `shipping` is a new state key in `RUN_DATA`, resource ->
  count.
- **Putting in:** `put` and `put_all` take a stack out of `held` at once.
  - It is all or nothing, as at the stall.
  - The bin takes only what the stall would buy, so money does not go in.
- **Paid at dawn:**
  - `due()` sums `Shop.paid_for` over the stacks: the sell price and the
    `sell_percent` bonus.
  - `Phases.begin_day` calls `pay()` after the stall restocks. The money
    lands, the bin empties, and the log says "the shipping bin paid $X".
- **What is in the bin is sold, not stock** (decided). A lost night takes a
  quarter of `held`; the bin is not touched and the morning pays for all of
  it.
- **The day stops while the bin is open** (decided), as at the stall:
  `open_panel` is `bin`. Choosing what to sell out of a full bag is the same
  conversation, only with nobody behind the counter.
- **The verb `ship`:**
  - it is in `OCCUPANT_VERBS`, `DAY_ONLY` and `ONE_SHOT`, and takes one tick;
  - its sound borrows `sfx/sell` until 0281, and its pose the trade strip;
  - `PlayerWork` gives it the stall's one-tick panel cue.

**The panel** (`ShopPanel`, in a bin mode). It reuses the stall's sell rows,
putting stacks in rather than selling them:
- **Text:**
  - title "SHIPPING BIN";
  - the morning's total where the money was: "in the bin: $X tomorrow";
  - a heading, "PUT IN - PAID AT DAWN", and no tabs;
  - the hint "esc to close the lid".
- **Keyboard and pad**, a way in the stall does not have:
  - The panel opens with the first live stack's `all` lit.
  - The arrows and the d-pad walk the rows.
  - SPACE, ENTER or A puts the stack in, and the light moves on when its
    row greys.
  - ESC or B closes it.
  - The scroll follows the light.
- **The stall itself is unchanged.**

**The morning report:**
- It gains the line "the shipping bin pays $X" (`RES_BIN`), from
  `Shipping.due`, the same sum `begin_day` pays.
- The line sits above the leftovers line, and only when the bin holds
  something.

**Names:** "shipping bin" / "caixa de envio" (`FIX_SHIPPING_BIN`), with the
`SHIP_*`, `RES_BIN` and `LOG_SHIPPED` rows in both languages.

**Art:**
- The stand-in is the barricade's planks, warmed and grown to a bin, until
  0215.
- A033's Deliverables state the settled geometry: one cell at (43,26), and
  24x24 at (12,22) for the closed bin and the three lid frames. 0215 plays
  the lid while the panel is open.

### Hashes

- **SIM 729970321 -> 3194686093, on purpose:**
  - the bin on the map;
  - the new `shipping` key;
  - `State.VERSION` 9.
- **DATA 2949384217 -> 1204968759, on purpose:** `FARM_MAP` has a `B` on the
  bin's site, and `MAP_LEGEND` the row that reads it.
